entries.section: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

paragraphs.text: The former account that St. Luke the Evangelist wrote to Theophilus, whose name means "lover of God," is the Gospel of Luke. It contains the important works in the life of the Lord and all His teachings concerning the salvation of mankind. Note that Christ acts before He teaches, because words are easy, whereas the deed, which is the accomplishment of redemption, is the hard part. The former account was about the life of Christ on earth, whereas what he is about to write here is the work of Christ through the Apostles after His Ascension.

entries.section: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

paragraphs.text: Here, in the Book of Acts, he will continue what the Lord resumed of His work and teaching after His ascension into heaven on the fortieth day after His holy Resurrection, and His commissioning of His disciples to preach the Gospel. Just as we must join words to deeds (v. 1), we must also make sure of the call of the Holy Spirit to us for service, through prayer and submission to the guidance of the Church.

Thus we see the continuity and connection between the Gospel, as the work of the Lord and His proclamation on earth, and the Book of Acts, as His work through His Apostles and disciples after His Ascension and by the Holy Spirit. Note that the Church reads the Synaxarium, which contains the saints of the day, after the Book of Acts, to declare that the word of the Lord grows, is strengthened and multiplies in His holy Church.

The position of the book between the Gospels and the Epistles links them together, because the Gospels are the life of Christ, the Book of Acts is the preaching of the Gospel, and the Epistles are how to live by it.

entries.section: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

paragraphs.text: Christ proved His Resurrection by His appearances to His disciples and to those who believed in Him. He proved to them that He is alive by eating with them, by their touching Him and by speaking with them. He broke the bread in the same manner as at the Last Supper when He was with the two disciples of Emmaus, and He worked miracles such as the great catch of fish at the Sea of Tiberias. So the disciples were certain that He was their Teacher Jesus Christ, who had lived with them for more than three years on earth. He spoke to them about the things pertaining to the Kingdom of God in the hearts of His children in the Church, that is, He delivered to them the faith and the various rites of worship, because the disciples are responsible for leading the ministry in His Church.

entries.section: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

paragraphs.text: While He was gathered with them, most likely toward the end of the forty days, He commanded them to return to Jerusalem and to stay there, because they had fled from it after the Crucifixion. He ordered them to wait for the descent of the Holy Spirit upon them, who is the promise of the Father, of whom the prophets prophesied, and of whom He had spoken to them many times during His life on earth.

entries.section: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

paragraphs.text: Christ informed them that they would be baptized with the Holy Spirit, as John the Baptist had prophesied, after a short time, about ten days, when the Holy Spirit would descend upon them.
This is a clear indication that the disciples were baptized before the rest of the believers.

entries.section: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

paragraphs.text: This is a gathering later than the one mentioned in (v. 4), for it took place on the very day of the Ascension. The disciples, like the rest of the Jews, thought that the kingdom of Christ was earthly; when He died their hopes were dashed, and then they were renewed by His Resurrection. When He promised them the descent of the Holy Spirit, they asked Him whether His kingdom on earth would be established on this day or later.

entries.section: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

paragraphs.text: Christ did not answer their question or their mistaken belief about His earthly kingdom, leaving this until after the Holy Spirit had come upon them, so that by His power He would guide them to understand that Christ's kingdom is spiritual. He charged them not to ask about the times when God will accomplish His purposes, especially the Second Coming, because if they knew that it was far off they would grow careless, or if it was near they would be terrified. They need only prepare spiritually for the service of God.

entries.section: (1) From the Resurrection to the Ascension

paragraphs.text: Christ assured them that the descent of the Holy Spirit would be accompanied by great power in the spiritual life and in service. They continued to bear witness for eight years in Jerusalem until King Herod killed the Apostle James, and then they preached in Judea, which is the southern part of the kingdom of the Jews, and Samaria, which is the middle part south of Galilee. In the days of His ministry on earth, Christ had forbidden them to preach in it because of their weakness before the obstinacy of the Samaritans, being content with His own ministry in Judea. After that He commanded them to preach to the whole world.
Does the work of the Holy Spirit, who dwells in you through the Myron, appear in your words and deeds, whatever your circumstances?
Ask for God's help, whatever the adverse circumstances around you, and the Holy Spirit will support you.

entries.section: (2) The Ascension and the return to the Upper Room

paragraphs.text: The Lord ascended in His body in the daytime before their eyes so that they would be sure of His ascension, and He disappeared in a cloud to confirm that He was lifted up into heaven and was not lost, to declare that His Kingdom is heavenly and that He went to prepare a place for us, so that we may lift up our hearts and prepare ourselves every day for heaven.

The cloud points to the presence of God, as happened when Moses received the commandments, and the cloud that covered the Tent of Meeting or Solomon's Temple when God came down and spoke with men, and as happened at the Transfiguration...

entries.section: (2) The Ascension and the return to the Upper Room

paragraphs.text: The eyes of the disciples remained fixed on heaven where Christ had entered in the midst of the cloud, their feelings either of sorrow at His departure, or of hope for His return shortly, or for some sign that would reveal His glory. While they were in this state, two angels suddenly appeared before them in the form of two men in bright white garments, to show the purity and majesty of heaven, and at the same time in the form of men so that the disciples would not be afraid of them. Their sudden appearance confirms that they were angels and not ordinary men.

entries.section: (2) The Ascension and the return to the Upper Room

paragraphs.text: The two angels spoke to the disciples in rebuke, because their eyes and hearts were still bound to Christ in the flesh, as He had lived among them on earth, and they were not yet able to live by faith and not by sight, although Christ had commanded them to stay in Jerusalem until the Holy Spirit came upon them, so that Christ would dwell in them and work more fully through the Holy Spirit.
They also informed them that Christ will come again on the Day of Judgment, so we must prepare for Him and live with Him, that we may rejoice on the last day.

entries.section: (2) The Ascension and the return to the Upper Room

paragraphs.text: The disciples returned to Jerusalem after the Ascension of Christ, which took place at the southeastern foot of the Mount of Olives, which is 2,000 paces from Jerusalem. This was the farthest distance the teachers of the Jews allowed a Jew to walk on the Sabbath, the day of rest, and they called it a Sabbath day's journey, because it is the distance between the farthest tent in the wilderness and the Tent of Meeting, so that they would permit walking it for a man to go to worship at the Tent of Meeting in ancient times.

entries.section: (2) The Ascension and the return to the Upper Room

paragraphs.text: The eleven continued in their prayers in the Upper Room in the house of the Apostle St. Mark, in spiritual unity. This is the fourth list of the names of the disciples, but Judas Iscariot is missing from it, who had hanged himself before this time.

There were with them women who followed Christ, whom the Gospels mention, such as Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, who was the sister of the Virgin, Salome the wife of Zebedee, Joanna the wife of Chuza, Susanna and others, all these in addition to the Virgin Mary, who had been living with John the Beloved since the Crucifixion of Christ. And His brethren: that is, the sons of His aunt, who believed in Him and became followers with the rest of the disciples. With one accord: for they were in fear of the Jews, in need of God's support, and longing to receive the power of the Holy Spirit whom Christ had promised them.
How pleasing it is to God that we pray in spiritual unity and with one accord in our homes and our churches, that the Lord may help His Church and His people.

So drive out of your heart all evil toward others, not only in the Divine Liturgy when you approach the Holy Mysteries, but also in your prayer in your inner room, that you may be of one accord with the rest of the believers, who are members of the Body of Christ.
Take care to feel for those around you and to pray for God's help for you all.

The number of believers in the house of St. Mark increased, whether from the seventy Apostles or those close to Christ, until it reached 120 persons. He called them disciples because all of them had become disciples and followed Christ during His life on earth. This does not mean that these were the only believers in Christ, but they were those close to Him, and so they include the eleven, the seventy Apostles, the Virgin Mary and the women who followed Christ, and perhaps Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus were with them.

They were praying in expectation of the descent of the Holy Spirit upon them. During their gathering Peter stood up to speak, because he was by nature inclined to zeal and initiative, and he was encouraged in this by being the eldest of them.

Peter said to them: The prophecies have been fulfilled, as David said in (Ps 41:9) concerning the betrayal of Judas Iscariot and his handing Christ over to the Jews, for he guided them to His place in the Garden of Gethsemane and they seized Him and crucified Him. Judas was one of the twelve disciples, and was being prepared to be an apostle preaching Christ to the whole world.

Here St. Luke adds information that did not appear in Peter's address, because Luke is speaking to Greeks who do not know the events that took place in Jerusalem, so he explains them to them: that with the price for which Judas sold Christ the priests bought a field, so that he is considered the buyer.
The reward of iniquity: that is, the price of selling Christ, the innocent and wronged.

St. Luke also mentions how Judas Iscariot took his own life: he went to the mountain and tied himself to a high rock or a tree at the edge of the mountain, and when his body's weight hung on the rope he was strangled. Then the weight of the body increased, so that the rock broke away from the mountain or the tree broke, and he fell from a great height, and his body burst open and his bowels gushed out. It was a hideous death, a proof of the greatness of his sin.
The gushing out of his bowels signifies the exposure of his inner sins, which were in his heart while he followed Christ in a show that was different from the evil he concealed within.

This story was known to all the Jews of Jerusalem, and this confirms that the words are Luke's and not Peter's, for there was no need for Peter to mention it, since his hearers knew it, being all Jews of Jerusalem. Their proper tongue: that is, the Syriac or Aramaic language that was widespread among the Jews.
Aceldama, the field of blood: an indication that it was the price of the blood of Christ.
David says in (Ps 69:25) and (Ps 109:8) concerning the traitor Judas that his house will be laid waste, that is, his memory will be abolished, and another apostle will take his ministry.

In denunciation by the Church of the betrayal of Judas, these words ("Let his habitation be desolate") are read to a special melody, and a procession is made in the reverse direction to another melody, on the morning of Holy Thursday.
Peter saw the necessity of choosing a replacement for Judas from among those close to Christ, who had been disciples at His hands throughout the period of His ministry on earth.
Went in... and out: that is, Christ mingled with them and associated with them, and they were disciples at His hands.
The baptism of John: that is, from the time Christ was baptized by John and began His ministry until He ascended into heaven. That is, those who witnessed His ministry on earth.

A witness of His resurrection: the foundation of the preaching of Christ was the proclamation of the redemption accomplished on the Cross and revealed in the power of His Resurrection. So one of the marks of an apostle is that he has seen Christ and witnessed His Resurrection, and even the Apostle Paul, Christ Himself appeared to him to declare His Resurrection to him.

The disciples chose two persons, Justus and Matthias, whose name means "gift of God." These two persons were distinguished among the followers of Christ in their righteousness. It seems that they were so close that the disciples could not prefer one over the other.
The disciples prayed to God, who knows the secrets of hearts, to choose by Himself which of the two He wanted as an apostle in place of Judas Iscariot.
Lots: that is, a portion.
Ministry and apostleship: that is, the apostleship that Judas left, to be taken by the one chosen by God, so that the disciples would again be twelve, as Christ had chosen them.
To his own place: that is, the wicked Judas going to the place of the wicked, which is hell.
Then they cast lots, and God chose Matthias to preach in the name of Christ.

May we always seek God's counsel before undertaking any important work, through prayer and humility before Him, for He alone knows our interest and our good and searches the hearts of men, so that He protects us and guides us to what benefits us, and we trust in Him and accept His guidance even if it runs contrary to our aims.
The descent of the Holy Spirit and the birth and life of the first Church

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Feast of Pentecost was one of the three great feasts among the Jews, namely Passover, Pentecost and Tabernacles, at which all males were required to be present in Jerusalem at the Temple. It came fifty days after the second day of the Feast of Passover and was called the Feast of Weeks or of Harvest, in which every Jew offered the firstfruits of his harvest, and it fell on a Sunday.
The hundred and twenty gathered in the Upper Room continued in prayer until this day with one accord.

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: In the house of St. Mark there came a sound like the sound of the wind, but coming from above and not from the distant horizon as we are accustomed to hear the wind (compare Jn 3:8). This sound was to alert the people to what was happening in the Upper Room.

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: What looked like fire appeared, formed into divided tongues, flying in the air and then resting upon the head of each one of those gathered in the Upper Room, as a sign of the fiery tongues in preaching that God would grant them, because fire is a symbol of purification and power.

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: When the tongues rested on each one of them, all were filled by the working of the Holy Spirit, and to show this each one of them spoke in a language he did not know, according to the divine promise (Mk 16:17). Thus three miracles appeared, namely the sound of the wind, the tongues of fire and speaking in strange languages, to declare the descent of the Holy Spirit and the founding of the Church.

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: Jews from the various countries of the world came and dwelt in Jerusalem to attend the Feast of Pentecost. They were among the devout who cared for worship, as proved by their enduring the hardships and expense of travel.

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: This noise: that is, the sound of the wind, so the Jews gathered together, the news spread, and great crowds assembled around the house.

It seems that those who had gathered went out of the Upper Room into the crowds thronging there, and each of them spoke in a language foreign to the prevailing language among the Jews, which was Aramaic. Those who knew this new language gathered around him and were in great bewilderment: how could men who were weak in education and culture speak so many foreign languages well, especially since they were all from Galilee and had not gone to the other countries of the world with their foreign languages? The hearers knew these languages well as a result of having grown up in them from childhood, but it was strange that these Galileans should suddenly know them.

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: St. Luke shows the greatness of the miracle by the multitude of languages in which they spoke. He mentioned the various countries of the world from which the Jews had come, each one with its own language, and arranged the countries from eastern Asia to its west, then Europe, then Africa, and then returned to Asia again.
Parthians, Medes and Elamites: they dwell near Iran.
Mesopotamia: that is, between the Tigris and the Euphrates, which is Iraq.

Judea: the southern part of the kingdom of the Jews. They represent the largest number of those gathered, and their language differed to some extent in pronunciation from the language of the people of Galilee.
Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia: these are countries in the region of present-day Turkey.
Egypt: present-day Egypt, which at this time spoke the Coptic language.
Libya and Cyrene: present-day Libya, and Cyrene is a city in it, lying in North Africa, west of Egypt.
Strangers of Rome: that is, Jews who settled in Italy, and their language is Latin.

Jews and proselytes: that is, Jews living in countries other than Judea, or Gentiles who joined the Jewish religion and so were called proselytes. Whether the one or the other, they came from the countries of the world, each with his own language. Cretes: the inhabitants of the island of Crete.
Arabians: they live in the Arabian Peninsula.
The wonderful works of God: those upon whom the Holy Spirit had come were speaking about Christ, His redemption, His Resurrection, and His holy salvation for the whole world.

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The hearers marveled at these languages and were bewildered in finding out the cause of this miracle: was it from God, or from some other cause?

entries.section: (1) The descent of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: Here the original Jews, who did not know these languages, began to mock, and thought that the Apostles and believers had drunk good wine, which is new wine.

Do not make light of the words of others or of any work they do, and do not hasten to judge it, but look for the good in it, and if you find a fault, find an excuse, so that your heart may be open to all and you win all, and at the same time keep your inner peace and your discernment of matters, far from tension and agitation.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: Here we see Peter, whom the power of the Holy Spirit had changed from fear to courage, standing with the eleven to preach to the Jews who lived in Jerusalem and to the guest Jews who had come for the feast, and asking them to listen to him.

He spoke in the Aramaic language, which all the hearers knew because all were Jews, explaining that the disciples and believers were not drunk, because it is impossible for a Jew, however great his wickedness, to drink wine before the prayer of the third hour, which is the first prayer among the Jews (Isa 5:7).

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: Rather, this event is the fulfillment of the prophecy of Joel (Joel 2:28-32).

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: Servants and handmaidens: he means those lowest in rank in society, whether the poor, the uneducated or the enslaved.

The Holy Spirit comes upon all believers, whatever their social standing, and the proof of His coming is prophesying, not only in announcing the future, but more especially preaching and teaching, because he speaks of things to come, which is the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: Blood: that is, the killing of many, as happened in the persecutions in the ages of martyrdom.
Fire: huge conflagrations, as Nero burned Rome and accused the Christians of it.
Vapor and smoke: resulting from the fires.
The sun shall be turned into darkness: this is a strong sign that occurs before the Day of Judgment, when the sun loses its light completely.

The moon into blood: that is, its color becomes like blood, and this is something very terrifying that will also take place before the Day of Judgment. These signs have happened and are happening in part, and then will be completed before the last Day of Judgment, and they signify spiritual meanings, since heresies arise against the divinity of Christ, the Sun of Righteousness, to deny Him, and distort the image of the Church, which is the moon, with the smoke of heresies.

The work of the Holy Spirit is not limited to the beautiful promises mentioned in (vv. 17, 18), but also includes threats. Disturbances in nature, afflictions and persecutions occur to lead people to repentance, such as the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70. These disturbances are a prelude to greater disturbances that will take place before the last Day of Judgment.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: God promised that whoever believes in Christ and repents of his sins will be saved, whether Jew or Gentile, that is, without distinction of race, and will escape all the preceding threats and receive the Kingdom of Heaven. It is clear that this verse is a comment on the preceding verses and cannot be separated from them, as claimed by the adherents of the heresy of universal salvation, who say that every person who calls upon the name of God is saved without faith in Christ or life in the Church. Thus they reject all the other verses of the Holy Bible that call for Baptism, Communion and all the spiritual practices of prayers and fasts...

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: God raised Him up: that is, the divinity united with His humanity. For Christ, in the form of weakness before the eyes of men, needed a power to raise Him, and that is the power of the divinity united with His humanity. Here he affirms that Christ is not separate from the God known to the Jews in the Old Testament, for it is He who raised Him because He and the Father are one, lest they fall into the heresy of two gods, one for the Old Testament and another for the New.

Peter explains to them that there are many proofs from the life of the Lord Christ showing that God worked miracles by His hand among them, and yet they seized Him and handed Him over to the Romans to kill Him.
In truth, that was the fulfillment of the counsel of God and His plan for the redemption of mankind by the death of Christ on the Cross.

Although it was the wicked hand of Pilate that issued the order for His crucifixion, they are the ones chiefly responsible for His crucifixion and death, because they demanded it and pressed Pilate to crucify Him. But God raised Him from the dead, and Christ triumphed over all the pangs that precede death, because He was stronger than death and it was impossible for death to subdue Him. This is the first time the Apostles preach the Resurrection, for Peter had changed from the weakness of denial, about fifty days before, to the courage of proclaiming and preaching by the power of the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: On my right hand: it signifies strength and confidence in Christ, so that He does not fear death because He is able to rise.
Glad and rejoicing... in hope: this shows that joy did not leave Christ during His sufferings because of His hope of rising from the dead.
You will not leave my soul in Hades: that is, in hell, the place where the wicked wait.
Nor allow Your Holy One to see corruption: that is, it is not possible for Christ the Holy One that His body should suffer any change or corruption like the rest of those who sleep in the tombs.
The ways of life: that is, the way out of death into life by the Resurrection, relying on the power of His divinity united with His humanity.

You will make me full of joy: this is the joy at the resurrection of mankind through His Resurrection, and then His ascension into glory, so that men who believe in Him have the ability, through His redemption, to enter the heavenly glories.

St. Peter the Apostle cites the prophecy of David the prophet (Ps 16), which David the prophet did not mean about himself, but spoke in the person of Christ while He was in the tomb with His divinity united to His body, so that He is not troubled by death because the divinity helps the humanity, and He returns by the Resurrection to His glory and His joy at the accomplishment of salvation and the announcing of this to His children.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: Let me freely speak: that is, it is permitted or possible or allowed.
The patriarch: because from his seed came all the fathers until Christ was born.
St. Peter affirms that it can easily be proved that David died and that his tomb is in Jerusalem.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: According to the flesh: that is, with respect to the human nature of Christ, but at the same time He has the divine nature united with His humanity.

This confirms that what David said as a prophet is not about himself but about Christ, when he was taught by the hand of Nathan the prophet in (2 Sam 7:12, 16), and declared it in the Psalm (Ps 89:3, 35-37), that Christ would be born of his seed according to the flesh. And indeed the Lord came from the seed of David.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: As David spoke in (Ps 16) of the Resurrection of Christ, and the triumph of His soul united with His divinity over Hades, and the preservation of His body united with His divinity from corruption until His soul returned to His body and He rose, as the Apostle Fathers testify.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: Christ was glorified before all and ascended into heaven, and sent the Comforter Spirit whom He had promised His disciples, on this day in this miraculous manner which they see, in the form of tongues of fire, the sound of the wind and speaking in tongues.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: All these words that David spoke do not apply to David himself either, but to Christ, for David did not ascend into heaven; rather it was he who conveyed by prophecy the conversation of the Father with the Son, which affirms the equality of the Son with the Father in essence and glory, because He said to Him, "Sit at My right hand," that is, after the accomplishment of redemption Christ returns to His glory in our sight, equal to the Father.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: This is the accomplishment of the goal of redemption, which is the confining of Satan in the lake of fire and brimstone (1 Cor 15:24-28), and thereby the enemies of Christ, that is, Satan and death, are subjected under His feet forever.

entries.section: (2) The sermon of the Apostle Peter

paragraphs.text: All the hearers must know and believe that the Lord Christ is the Lord and Savior.
The Holy Spirit, who changed Peter from weakness to strength and to witness to Christ, is able to lift you from your weakness, whatever your sins, so that you may walk in purity.
Submit to Him by repentance, asking for His help, and partaking of the Holy Mysteries, and you will be strengthened in all your steps.

entries.section: (3) The faith and Baptism of the multitudes

paragraphs.text: When they heard, they were deeply moved in the depths of their hearts and asked the Apostles for guidance as to what they should do, declaring their repentance and their readiness to carry out what the Spirit says on the tongues of the Apostles.

entries.section: (3) The faith and Baptism of the multitudes

paragraphs.text: St. Peter answered, asking them to repent, to change their way, to declare their faith in Christ the Savior, one with His Father and the Holy Spirit, and to receive the sacrament of Baptism, so that their sins would be forgiven them and the Holy Spirit would come upon them.
Here we note the work of Baptism in the forgiveness of sins and the renewal of man's nature, for it is a condition for acceptance into Christianity.

entries.section: (3) The faith and Baptism of the multitudes

paragraphs.text: Those who are afar off: that is, the Gentiles, for this is a proclamation that salvation is for the Jews and the Gentiles.
As many as the Lord our God shall call: by means of the preachers and servants.

The Apostle declared to them that the promise of eternal life is for everyone who repents, believes and is baptized, whether of the Jews or their children, who can also be baptized. For this reason the Church baptizes infants.

entries.section: (3) The faith and Baptism of the multitudes

paragraphs.text: The Apostle continued at length in his sermon (not all of which is recorded in this book), bearing witness to the Lord and calling the hearers to accept Christ the Savior and to turn away from the crooked works of the wicked.

entries.section: (3) The faith and Baptism of the multitudes

paragraphs.text: They received the word with joy and believed, repenting and being baptized. Thus the Church was born on the day of Pentecost, and the grain of wheat (that is, Christ), which died and rose, began to bring forth much fruit, which was three thousand souls.

When your heart is moved by the word of God, turn it into action through repentance and a serious way of life, with a self-giving love toward those around you, and submit to the fathers and guides, and you will know how to walk in righteousness and purity.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: Here we see the steadfastness of the new believers in the Lord, continuing in four basic things that distinguished the new community, which are:
1- Listening to the teaching of the Apostles.
2- Fellowship, that is, the love feast, which expresses unity.
3- The breaking of bread, that is, Communion from the Body and Blood of the Lord.
4- Corporate liturgical prayers, that is, the Liturgy.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: The fear of God came into the souls of the believers, which made them keep away from sins and walk in purity, and likewise the Jews and the pagans feared the Church as a community full of zeal and power. God supported them with miracles to confirm their faith and call many to believe in Christ.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: The believers met together with one accord and love, which drove them not only to pray together but to consider what they owned as belonging to the Church, so that they distributed it to all, and what they had they could give to the Church at any time, because they were all members of the Body of Christ.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: Many sold their possessions and divided the money among all according to their need, especially since many Jews who had come from the whole world to attend the Feast of Pentecost had settled in Jerusalem after accepting the faith, and they had no source of livelihood in the Jewish land.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: Worship in the Temple was in Solomon's Porch beside the Beautiful Gate, the only ancient part of the Temple that was not demolished at the exile since Solomon built it. They kept the unity of the Spirit, and besides this they prayed and celebrated the sacrament of the Eucharist in the houses, rejoicing in the Lord in whom they had believed and who had given them simplicity of heart.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: The believers were distinguished by praising and thanking God with joy, so the Jews loved them because of the purity of their conduct and their compassion for the poor. This helped the Holy Spirit bring many to faith every day.
Do you feel your union in the Church with the rest of the believers, so that you take care to attend the Liturgies and the spiritual meetings?

And do you seek to meet the needs of others and feel that all you own belongs to God and the Church? If you do this, then God will keep you in a pure life and give you favor in the eyes of those around you. The healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate

The Jews prayed three times a day: the third hour (9 a.m.), the sixth (12 noon) and the ninth (3 p.m.). The early Church in its beginning prayed at the same times in Solomon's Porch at the Temple, though of course without taking part in its sacrifices, until the prayers of the Agpeya and other Church prayers became settled in about the fourth century. Peter and John: these two disciples were joined together from the beginning of Christ's call to them and in special events such as the Transfiguration, the raising of Jairus' daughter, the Garden of Gethsemane and the Sea of Tiberias. The ninth hour: the hour at which Christ gave up the Spirit and completed our redemption, so we go out in it to preach by His power, which is able to work miracles.

At the gate of the Temple there was a man lame from his mother's womb, that is, born unable to walk, who was then more than forty years old. His family would carry him and set him at the "Beautiful" gate of the Temple to beg all day long, as is the custom of the poor at the entrances of houses of worship. The Beautiful Gate is the most beautiful of the nine gates that were in the Temple, and this gate was made of bronze and overlaid with gold leaf. Its location was on the eastern side of the Temple between the court of judgment and the court of the Gentiles. Because of the beauty of its appearance, most of those coming to the Temple preferred to enter by it, which is why the lame man sat there to seek his livelihood.
Peter and John saw the lame man, and he asked them for alms as usual, since he did not know them and did not expect healing from them.
The two Apostles looked intently at him and asked him to fix his gaze and thought on what would be given to him. It was not merely alms but something greater, namely healing and faith.
The man thought that he would receive a large sum of money in alms.

They had no money, because Christ did not promise His children that He would give them money, but precious spiritual blessings that money cannot buy. The two Apostles used the power of Christ and asked for his healing in His name.
Here we note the difference between the miracles of Christ, which He worked by His direct command, and the miracles of the saints, which they work in the name of the Lord.
The lack of money with you does not mean that you cannot give, for Chrysostom says: The woman had two mites with which she bought the Kingdom. And do you not have two eyes, two feet and two hands?
Almsgiving can be a deed or a word, and not money only.
He took him: this shows God's help, the tenderness of the two Apostles and the power of support for everyone in need.

His feet and ankle bones received strength: this shows the obedience of the lame man and his will to carry out what the two Apostles commanded him, so he felt a power flowing in his muscles when he tried to rise, and he was able to stand, and even walk and leap. Leaping: jumping with joy, and he entered the Temple amid the crowd of those gathered to offer the evening sacrifice at the ninth hour.

The miracle was accomplished immediately. After his healing the man was amazed, and began to walk and leap and thank God for what He had done with him, and he also clung to the company of the two Apostles.

The miracle became clear to everyone, because the crowd saw him walking and thanking God, especially since those present had known for many years that he was lame; so they were bewildered and greatly astonished, asking how this had happened to him.
Thus the saying of Isaiah about the miracles of the New Testament is fulfilled: "Then shall the lame man leap as an hart" (Isa 35:6).

"The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10). So we have protection and strength by repeating it always in prayer - "My Lord Jesus Christ, help me" - and He gives us blessing and salvation, protects us from the wars of the devil and gives us strength to overcome difficulties.
Solomon's Porch: a large colonnade running along the back (eastern) wall of the Temple, with 162 columns.

After his healing the man clung to the two Apostles, in acknowledgment of their kindness and to learn from them about the Lord Jesus, in whom he had newly believed. All entered Solomon's Porch, and great crowds from the Temple and the city followed them when they heard the news. His presence with the two Apostles was a proclamation of the miracle and a preaching of the power of Christ, which is able to do all things.

The Apostle Peter seized the opportunity of the gathering of many to see the miracle, and at once answered the questions of the people, and stressed emphatically that he and John were not the authors of the miracle of healing, but the Lord Jesus Christ Himself, who is one with His good Father.
If you do something good and others praise you for it, thank God and turn the glory to Him, so that all hearts may be attached to Him, and you disappear and He appears.

The God of our fathers: that is, the God known in the Old Testament to all the Jews. And Jesus Christ is His Son, and not a prophet or merely an ordinary person. So he proclaims the divinity of Christ, His redemption and the need to believe in His salvation.
Glorified His Son: by His Resurrection and Ascension.
You denied Him in the presence of Pilate: that is, your insistence on rejecting Christ, although His miracles and His words proclaim His divinity, and even Pilate himself testified to His innocence.

He told them that the God of the fathers - Abraham, Isaac and Jacob - from whose descendants these hearers came, has glorified His Son Jesus in the healing of the lame man in His name. And this Jesus is the one they refused to believe in, and they refused to let Pilate release Him, though he had satisfied himself of His innocence when he tried Him.
The Jews asked that Barabbas the murderer be released to them instead of Jesus, when Pilate offered them the release of Christ on the occasion of the Feast of Passover.

Thus they held fast to a murderer, Barabbas, and rejected the Source of life and demanded His death. But the Father raised Him from the dead, which the Apostles bear witness to, for they saw Him with their own eyes after His Resurrection, and ate and lived with Him for forty days.
Raised from the dead: this is a proclamation of His divinity and that He is the Source of life, whereas they preferred the taker of life, that is, Barabbas.

Here we see the central place of the Resurrection in preaching, since there is no Christianity without the Resurrection. We also see the Apostles' complete denial of themselves and their seeking only the glory of Christ.
Through faith in His name: the faith of the two Apostles and likewise the faith of the lame man.

Perfect soundness: that is, the strength of the two legs that for more than forty years had been unable to stand or walk. The Apostle Peter declares that the basis of the accomplishment of the miracle is faith, in order to call the hearers to faith in Christ the Savior, who is able to heal our diseases and solve all our problems.

He gently makes an excuse for them because they were ignorant of the person of Christ, since they and their rulers demanded His crucifixion. For the preacher is careful to remove the spirit of despair from the soul of the hearer, lest he despair of himself, and to make it easy for him to come to repentance so that his sins are forgiven.

What they did was useful for the fulfillment of God's counsel concerning the salvation of mankind, which all the prophets of the Old Testament foretold, especially Isaiah, who saw by the spirit of prophecy the Lord wounded for our transgressions (Isa 53:5). Thus the Father, the Maker of good things, turned the evil of the Jews into salvation and good.

What is required of them now, and likewise of us, is repentance and turning back from walking in evil, and confession of the faith, so that they may receive Baptism and their sins be forgiven, as the list of debts is blotted out when they are paid. And the times of refreshing come from the presence of God, because the Jews imagined that the coming of Christ would bring material relief and deliverance from the hand of the Romans. But what is meant here is spiritual refreshing by being delivered from the hand of Satan.

He shall send: what is meant is either the Incarnation of Christ to give us salvation in the New Testament so that we live by faith in Him, or His Second Coming to take His children and glorify them with Him in heaven. Which before was preached: that is, the One of whom the prophets of old prophesied that He would come and save the world.

Heaven must receive Him: the Jews believed that the Christ would remain on earth forever, that is, that He would not die, so they wondered at His words about the necessity of His death (Jn 12:34). Peter explained that Christ remains alive forever, but in heaven and not on earth.

The times of restitution of all things: that is, the spread of the proclamation of Christ in the whole world and the faith of many. It does not mean that by restitution of all things every soul will be received, but those appointed by God and prepared for salvation. Christ ascended to the Father and is in heaven until the end of the times arrives, in which the world returns to the knowledge of Christ and faith in Him (1 Cor 15:25), and then after that comes His Second Coming at the end of the world, as the holy prophets foretold.

The Apostle pointed to the prophecy of Moses the prophet about the Lord Christ in (Deut 18:18), who comes as a prophet, that is, one who makes known the will of the Father for the salvation of the world, and as being like Moses in respect of:
1- Prophecy.
2- His bringing the law of the New Testament, as Moses brought the law of the Old Testament.
3- His delivering His people from the hand of Satan, as Moses delivered the people from the bondage of Pharaoh.
4- His atoning intercession for His people, like Moses' pleading intercession for the Jews many times so that God would not destroy them in their murmurings in the wilderness.

Moses asked them to believe in Christ and listen to His message, because they believe that they are the sons of Moses, so it is necessary for them to believe in Christ, of whom he prophesied among them, and not to oppose Him and despise Him as they said to the man born blind (Jn 9:28, 29).

For whoever does not hear Christ is deprived of membership in the new people of God, that is, the Church, and will have no inheritance in the Kingdom, that is, he perishes. He proclaimed the punishment of unbelief in order to call them to repentance and salvation.

He also affirmed that Samuel, who was the first prophet after Moses and who founded the school of the prophets, also prophesied about the Lord, he and all who came after him of the prophets of the Old Testament up to John the Baptist, and their prophecies included the descent of the Holy Spirit and the working of the miracles that take place in the days of the New Testament.
Children of the prophets: that is, followers, so they must believe what the prophets foretold about Christ.

Your seed: that is, Christ, as the Apostle Paul explained (Gal 3:16), and he urged them, as children of the covenant that God gave of old to Abraham their father, by the coming of Christ from his seed, blessing and saving all people, Jews and Gentiles.

The Jews had priority in receiving faith in the coming of Christ to them first, before the Gentiles, so that through faith in Him they might receive the spiritual blessings that make them leave their sins for a life of repentance. This sermon resembles the sermon of Pentecost in the following:
1- The proof that Jesus of Nazareth is the awaited Messiah.
2- The showing of the sin of the Jews in rejecting Christ.
3- A call to repentance to receive the mercy of God and to believe in Christ.
All of us are exposed to sin, but we are distinguished from others by repentance, returning to God and repairing what we have spoiled by our sins.
May we not oppose the guidance others give us, nor what we hear in the Church and the Holy Bible, for they are personal messages that call us to repentance and rescue us from error.

Let us have daily repentance that renews our life and restores our spiritual zeal, and let us complete it in the sacrament of Confession, so that we always live by repentance and receive our salvation.
The trial of Peter and John, the power of prayer and the life of the first Church

entries.section: (1) The imprisonment of the two Apostles

paragraphs.text: The priests: they had authority to permit or forbid teaching in the Temple to whomever they wished.
The news of the preaching inside Solomon's Porch reached the priests, so they came at once, and with them the captain of the Temple guard and his soldiers, who were Jewish Levites and not Romans.

The Sadducees also came, who do not believe in the Resurrection, and because they regarded what the Apostles said about the Resurrection of Christ as an attack on their beliefs, they were the fiercest opponents of the Apostles' preaching. All of them were displeased at the spread of the news of the Resurrection of Christ, which they had tried to conceal by bribing the Roman soldiers at the tomb.

entries.section: (1) The imprisonment of the two Apostles

paragraphs.text: They seized the two Apostles, and since they wanted to gather the seventy elders, the members of the supreme Jewish council, the "Sanhedrin," some of whom lived outside Jerusalem, they put the Apostles in custody until the next day so that the gathering of the members could be completed.

entries.section: (1) The imprisonment of the two Apostles

paragraphs.text: The opposition of the priests and Sadducees did not stop the effect of the two Apostles' proclamation on the people, for the number of believers increased and became five thousand men, and this rapid growth of the Church was a clear fruit of the Holy Spirit.

Do not be disturbed by the opposition of the wicked, but hold fast to your principles and the commandments of Christ, for their mockery and opposition, however strong it may seem, is a test of your faith and steadfastness, and trust in God's blessing on your personal life and even in the effect of your words and conduct on others, though it be after a while.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: The next day the three groups that make up the council gathered, namely: the rulers, that is, the priests; the elders, that is, the heads of the clans; and the scribes, that is, the scholars and teachers. They gathered in Jerusalem to try the two Apostles.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: And Annas was with them: the former high priest, whom the Romans had removed.
Caiaphas: the current high priest.
John and Alexander: relatives of the high priest and men of standing in Jerusalem.
The kindred of the high priest: five high priests came out of it, so it was a distinguished clan, and from it, accordingly, came a large number of members of the Sanhedrin.
All these gathered to stop the preaching of the risen Christ, because this would reveal their wickedness in condemning Christ to death.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: They set the two Apostles in the midst, and the question was repeated about the source of the power that worked the miracle and about the name by which the miracle was accomplished. This was not because they did not know the answer, but so that they might find in the answer an opportunity to seize on against the Apostles in order to punish them, regarding the use of the name of Christ as a kind of blasphemy or sorcery. The purpose of setting them in the midst and questioning them was to intimidate them so that they would stop their preaching.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: Here the Lord's promise in (Mt 10:19-20) is fulfilled, that when a Christian is tried for the faith the Holy Spirit speaks on his tongue.

Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit and went straight to the subject with all courage, to make up for his denial of the Lord during the trial at the high priest's house, and he addressed them with the respect due to them.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: A good deed: trials are held because of a wrong, but now it is held because of a good deed and help done to another, and this shows the wickedness of the Sanhedrin.
This is because the lame man who was healed was present at the trial.

They must know, and all the Jews with them, that the name of the Lord Jesus, who is the Christ, the awaited Messiah, who is of Nazareth, as they wrote on His cross, and who rose from the dead by the power of the Father against their plan, this name is what healed the sick man. So Peter, who was foremost in speaking, expressing his own opinion and John's, showed three basic matters that call the hearers to faith, which are:
1- Jesus of Nazareth is the Christ.
2- Their sin in condemning Him to the cross.
3- In the name of Christ the lame man was healed and stood, and he is standing before them now.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: The chief cornerstone: it is the highest stone in any arch or dome bearing a roof, upon which falls all the pressure from the stones of the arch on its right or its left, so that the arch does not collapse. Or it is the stone that joins two walls meeting at a right angle.
What is meant is that Christ is the foundation of salvation for mankind, and none other.

The builders: the members of the council of the seventy, who were responsible for the spiritual building of the Jews, and who ought to have been the first to believe in Christ so as to lead the people in the way of faith.

Peter completed his preaching to them. We note that he does not defend himself or John but preaches the Lord, pointing out their error, which the Psalm (Ps 118:22) mentioned, in rejecting faith in Christ Jesus and despising Him, whereas God made Him the chief cornerstone in the cause of the accomplishment of salvation.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: Christ alone is the Savior and He alone is the One anointed by God to accomplish salvation, for He alone possesses the atoning intercession that forgives the sins of His people and atones for their evils.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: They marveled greatly at the power of the preaching, and the mention of the boldness of John is noted, so it is understood implicitly that he supported Peter's words with words and gestures proclaiming his faith, although the two Apostles had not been taught under the teachers of the Jews or in their religious schools, but were of the common people. From this the chief priests remembered that the two Apostles had been with Christ, and had seen them with Him before, so He is the source of their knowledge and eloquence.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: The presence of the sick man who was healed left them no opportunity to oppose the two Apostles, and the judges became the accused in their opposition to Christ.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: They had them taken out of the council to confer and issue the verdict, and instead of asking themselves what to do about their own salvation and their attitude toward this preaching, they concentrated their wickedness on how and what to do with the Apostles, now that the effect of this clear sign had reached the minds of the people of Jerusalem.

So a man grows hardened by sin when he becomes accustomed to it. What they did to Christ of injustice they wanted to apply to the Apostles, because their personal dignity was what they were after, not the truth. So if your error becomes apparent, do not continue to resist or to justify yourself, but return to God in prayer that He may reveal the truth to you, so that you repent and correct your mistakes, following the example of Saul of Tarsus, who obeyed and became the great Apostle Paul.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: They decided to threaten them so that they would be afraid to resume preaching among the people and would not mention the name of Jesus, which they could not even bear to pronounce with their mouths. For, being unable to find any charge against them, they used threats to frighten them.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: They brought them back into the session and charged them not to repeat such preaching in the future.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: But the two Apostles replied that God must be obeyed rather than men, and it is He who commands them to preach the Gospel to the whole world, and therefore they cannot keep silent about what they had seen or heard in the days of Christ's companionship with them. Here appear:
1- The evil purposes of the council against the commands of God.
2- The obedience of the two Apostles to God and their strength in holding to the truth, whatever the opposition.

entries.section: (2) The trial of Peter and John

paragraphs.text: So they were released without punishment for fear of the people, who were glorifying God for the miracle, especially since this man had been sick for more than forty years. The length of the illness and the inability of human medicine to cure it shows the power of the miracle.
And so the council had nothing but threats, because it was powerless before the power of God.

The clear truths of God are before us, but our pride prevents us from confessing our sins and accepting the saving work of God in us. It is our duty not to lose the opportunity like these rulers, who lived in the illusion of putting an end to the preaching rather than responding to it.

After their release the two Apostles returned to the Apostles and the rest of the believers and told them what had happened, to strengthen their faith, to thank God and to rejoice in His work in His Church.

In view of their great need of God's help, they prayed fervently, calling upon God the Creator of all things and the One able to protect His children, as we address Him in the Liturgy with this prayer, "that He is the Creator of all that exists." Thus we see that prayer is the greatest solution to man's weakness and problems.

For as long as God is the Creator of the universe and its Ruler, our hearts are reassured, whatever the threats of the wicked. This prayer is also a prayer of thanksgiving to God for His great grace and His rescue of His Apostles.

Those gathered prayed to God, who said by the mouth of David the prophet in the Psalm (Ps 2:1, 2) that many would rise up against Christ with their thoughts and their opposing deeds, whether rulers or kings, stubbornly resisting the Lord (the Father) and His Christ (the Son). This is what happened with the rulers of the Jews in their opposition to Christ and the Apostles, and this shows the power of God and the weakness of the rulers of the world and their turmoil because of the evil in their hearts, and the failure of all their plots, because God is stronger than they: if they crucify Christ, He rises on the third day victorious, and if they seize the Apostles, they find no charge against them, but the miracle spreads and draws many to faith.

Were gathered together against Your holy Child: this was fulfilled before the two Apostles in what they saw of the priests and the council of the Jews moving against Christ, together with Herod and Pilate and many of the Gentiles and Jews. But God, the Ruler of all, allowed what happened because it was the accomplishment of His plan for the salvation of mankind.

They did not ask the Lord to protect them, but to strengthen them for the success of the preaching with all clarity and boldness. This shows their great attachment to Christ the Savior and their faith in Him and their desire to spread the faith, so they do not think of themselves but ask for power by which to glorify God.

They also asked Him to support them with other miracles of healing and signs confirming the truth of their preaching, and wonders bearing witness to the greatness of the name of Christ, the Holy One, the Son of the Great God.

Then a visible sign appeared of the acceptance of their prayer by God, which was the shaking of the place and the filling of those present with the Spirit, that is, the Holy Spirit gave them strength to continue and work, and they received zeal and power to proclaim the name of Christ and preach Him.

The first descent, for the beginning of the Spirit's dwelling in man, is not repeated, but the filling, to renew his activity and work, can be repeated many times in proportion to the purity of man's soul and his asking for the filling from God.
Take refuge in God through prayer in all your needs, confident of His support.
Thank Him for His gifts and ask for more for His name's sake, and you will receive abundantly, for He is rich and loves His children and will help you to show His name in your life and your words.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: Here he calls the believers a multitude, since they had increased beyond the five thousand mentioned before, but all had the unity of the one Holy Spirit, the leader and guide of each individual and of the whole group. They still lived by the principle of common ownership without selfishness, for each one felt that his money belonged to the Church and to all in it.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: The Spirit was working in the Apostles with power to preach the Resurrection of Christ, which is the foundation of faith in Christ the Savior. As for the great grace that came upon them all, it gave their preaching an extraordinary power and penetration in the hearts of the hearers, who saw them in intense love, for there was not one poor person among them but complete harmony between rich and poor, as the owners of fields and possessions hastened to sell them to meet the needs of those in need.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: Laying the money at the feet of the Apostles was a figure of the believers' lack of concern for it, for their hearts were occupied with the spiritual life, while material needs were of less importance, and all money was counted as nothing before faith and life with God. So money was used to meet the needs of all according to each one's situation.

entries.section: (4) The life of the first Church

paragraphs.text: This also included one of the well-known servants, Joseph, the uncle of the Apostle St. Mark, whom the Apostles called Barnabas, that is, son of exhortation, because of the eloquence and the moving words that distinguished him among the hearers. He was originally of the tribe of Levi, among those living abroad in Cyprus, and he owned a field, which he sold and gave its price to the Apostle Fathers.

May you feel for the needy around you and know well that all the money and possessions you have belong to God, who appointed you steward over them to meet your needs and the needs of those around you. You are a member of the Body of Christ, which is the Church, so do not shut up your compassion from any person in need.
The growth of the Church and the trials
This is an example of a trial that afflicts the Church from within, unlike the persecutions by the leaders of the Jews that afflicted it from outside.
Behold Ananias, whose name means "the Lord's grace," and Sapphira his wife, whose name means "shining," sell a field for the need of the Church, as many were doing.

But they wanted to hide part of the price and keep it for themselves while claiming that what they would give to the Apostles was the whole price. They agreed on this and carried it out out of love of appearing generous and giving lavishly, though it was their right to keep one part and give the other. But it was the sin of hypocrisy and love of show that led to the lie, and by their lie they are counted as thieves of part of God's money, which they claimed to have given to Him, namely the whole price of the field.

Peter declared to Ananias the gravity of his yielding to Satan, who had filled his heart with love of show, and this means that Ananias could have driven out the evil thoughts of Satan but was negligent because of his pride. This perhaps also shows the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit, for He is one of the hypostases of the Trinity and not merely the power of God, as claimed by the heretic Macedonius, whom the Church calls the enemy of the Holy Spirit and who was anathematized by the Council of Constantinople.
Conceived this thing in your heart: that is, he intended evil or planned the intention for it.

Peter explained to Ananias that he had the right to dispose of his property as he wished, so he need not sell the field if he did not want to, and likewise he could give all its price or part of it. The Apostle rebuked him for his lie because it was directed to God before men.

Know that every sin we commit against a person is directed first toward God, as David the prophet said, "Against thee, thee only, have I sinned" (Ps 51:4). So do not forget the presence of God, but for His sake keep away from sin so as not to anger Him, and remind yourself that He stands before you and sees all your deeds, words and thoughts, and even if you fall, hasten to repent to Him and He will forgive you and you will escape all punishment.

God's punishment was immediate, with the death of Ananias as he fell, which put the fear of God in the hearts of the believers. This was necessary at the beginning of the Church so that they would reject sin and be careful about their lives, and it also gave awe to the Apostles, for they had the gift of revealing the unseen, so the Holy Spirit gave Peter to know what Ananias and his wife Sapphira had done.

If you suffer from laziness and negligence, remember the judgment of God so that you fear Him and keep away from sin, for love alone is not enough for your salvation, but also the fear of God and the rejection of the sin that causes your destruction. This is why the Church reminds you every day before you sleep, in the prayer of sleep in the Agpeya, that you will stand before the just Judge, so that you feel terrified and trembling because of your many sins, and it leads you to repentance and the salvation of your soul and you enjoy the sweetness of fellowship with Him and His overflowing love.
The young men buried Ananias outside the city of Jerusalem, in which the Jews did not allow anyone to be buried.

The gathering of the believers continued for three hours, during which Ananias was buried, and after that his wife Sapphira came, not knowing what had happened to her husband, but thinking that the deceit and lie they had agreed on had succeeded.

The price of the field was still laid before the Apostles when Sapphira came in, so Peter hastened to ask her whether this sum was the whole price of the field, to give her an opportunity to repent and declare the truth, but unfortunately she persisted in the lie she had agreed on with her husband.

Do not indulge others in breaking God's commandments, lying so that they will not be angry with you, or agreeing to any sin and sharing in it, such as condemnation or foul words... You are responsible for every word that comes out of your mouth.
May you take care to please God before pleasing men.
To tempt the Spirit of the Lord: by Ananias and Sapphira doubting the ability of the Apostles to uncover the truth of their deceit through the Holy Spirit.
The feet of them which have buried your husband: that is, the young men were about to arrive at the place of the gathering after burying Ananias.
The Apostle Peter declares the agreement of the couple in evil and consequently the necessity of punishment falling on them.
Sapphira fell down dead, and the young men who had buried her husband arrived and carried her out to bury her.
All feared God, whether they were members of the Church or the rest of the Jews in Jerusalem.
Here in the Book of Acts the word "church" is used for the first time.
Miracles took place at the hands of the Apostles confirming the truth of their message openly before all the people. And all of them, in unity of the Spirit, prayed in Solomon's Porch.
As for those outside the faith, they feared the believers and the Apostles and held them in honor because of their purity and the power of God working in them.

New believers continued to join, and their number was not mentioned as it was the last time, when he said five thousand, because the number had greatly increased. He made clear here what he had not made clear before, that they were men and women, to show the importance of woman, like man, in the Church.
Beds: soft, furnished couches suitable for the rich.
Couches: rough, and used by the poor.

The sick, rich (carrying them on beds) and poor (laying them on couches), were healed by the mere falling of the shadow of the Apostle Peter on them, without his even touching them. For God wanted to show the power of His Holy Spirit in His Apostles, in that their shadow alone was enough to heal diseases, especially since the number crowded around them seeking healing was very great.

The healing of the sick was not limited to the residents of Jerusalem, but included also those coming from the cities around it. And it was not only healing of diseases, but also casting out demons and healing all the various diseases that result from these unclean spirits. The power of the Holy Spirit appears in the Apostles, who had been unable to heal the epileptic from the unclean spirit at the Mount of Transfiguration (Mt 17:19), whereas now by touch or even by shadow they are able to heal all diseases and cast out demons.

The Holy Spirit who dwells in you calls you to adorn yourself with virtues and to serve those around you, so respond to His voice and do not neglect it, and then you will be a light to the world around you, and they will see the power of God and His grace in you as it was with the Apostles.

Satan stirred up the high priest and all his followers of the Sadducees who deny the Resurrection, and the teachings of the Apostles confirming the Resurrection of Christ enraged them, so they were intensely jealous for their mistaken beliefs and seized the Apostles and put them in the prison of Jerusalem. Naturally the Apostles raised their voices in prayer to God to save them and support them.
The Temple: most likely in Solomon's Porch, the most conspicuous place where the people gather, so that they might preach Christ without fear.

All the words of this life: that is, the proclamation of Christ by which we live in the world and which extends with us into eternity. An angel of the Lord came by night and opened the prison door and brought them out, then returned and shut it and asked them to go and complete the preaching. Their going out of the prison was not an escape from it, but in order to complete their ministry in the Temple, preaching eternal life.

Thus we see that the Christian's completion of his mission is more important to him than the safety of his life, because he knows that his remaining on earth is for the accomplishment of his preaching of Christ.

So take care to proclaim the truth even if you are exposed to the words and insults of those who oppose, confident of the power of God that supports you. Only seek God before you speak, that He may guide you and give you wisdom as to when and how to speak.

The Apostles entered the Temple at once in the morning, at the time when it was full of Jews who had come to say the morning prayer, and began to preach Jesus and the Resurrection, heedless of their weariness and exhaustion from keeping vigil all night in prison, because their hearts were attached to the love of God, which sustained their weak bodies. At the same time the high priest and his followers - of the Sadducees - called the members of the Sanhedrin to meet, together with all the elders of the Jews. The purpose was to punish the Apostles to prevent their preaching, so that they would thereby be rid of the preaching of Christ and this story, which troubled them, would end.
And when the council assembled they sent their servants to bring the Apostles from the prison, for they did not know that the Apostles were in the Temple.
When the servants, that is, the soldiers of the Temple, opened the prison, they found no one in it, though it had been securely locked and the guards stood before the doors.
This confirms that what happened was by the hand of an angel and not a man, and the power of God appears, which made the prison guards not feel the Apostles going out, for they were in deep sleep.
The captain of the Temple guard and the chief priests fell into perplexity and doubt, being unable to explain what had happened.

Their confusion increased when they learned that the Apostles were standing firm and had not fled, but were teaching the people in the Temple. This means their insistence on preaching in the name of Christ, rejecting the orders of the chief priests.

The captain of the Temple guard went with his soldiers and brought the Apostles without violence, fearing for their own lives, in view of the people's honor and respect for the Apostles; for if they used violence with them the Apostles would not resist them, but the people would have struck them down and stoned them.
When they stood before the council, the high priest asked them why they had disobeyed his command and continued to teach in the name of Christ. We note two things here:
He did not ask them about the miracle of their being brought out of the prison, as though it did not concern him because he refuses to believe.

He would not consent to mention the name of Christ with his tongue, so he called Him "this man," as if He were a nobody without a name, out of the excess of his hatred of Him, and his distress that the Apostles' preaching of the risen Christ exposes the error of the priests who killed Him and brings His blood upon them, forgetting what they themselves said in (Mt 27:25), "His blood be on us, and on our children."

Peter and all the Apostles declared that the commands of God, which are the words of Christ to them and what the angel commanded them, are more important than the words of men, even if they are the greatest council among the Jews, the Sanhedrin.
The Apostles said that God, the God of all the fathers in whom the Jews believe, has raised up Christ, whom they wronged and crucified.

God exalted Christ by His high divine power as Head of the Church and Savior of the whole world, calling to repentance and granting forgiveness to all believers of the Jews, since the preaching was to them first, before the Gentiles.
This is the witness of the Apostles and the witness of the Holy Spirit, who fills them as believers in Christ who obey Him.
Our observation is repeated, that witness to Christ is the center of the life of those who believe in Him in every time and place.

The Apostles seized the opportunity of their trial before the Sanhedrin to preach Christ to them, in the hope that they might repent. So do good and show love to everyone, however harsh and however much he rejects the word of God. If you show love to the beloved brother, then show manifold more to the one who wrongs you and opposes you, for he needs love more than others do, and do not despair of anyone's salvation.
As a result of the high priest's intense anger, he consulted with his followers about killing all the Apostles in order to be finished with this matter.
The Law: that is, the Torah, which is the five books of Moses.
Commanded: so that the anger of the Sadducees might subside and they might accept his words. For he was a Pharisee who believed in the Resurrection, and it seems that he was moderate and wise.

God used one of the great teachers of the Jews, Gamaliel, the son of Simeon the elder, who carried the Lord in his arms when He was presented at the Temple at the age of 40 days, and who was in turn the son of Hillel, the great Jewish teacher. Gamaliel was a man of honor and clear intellectual wisdom, and Saul of Tarsus was taught at his hands. He ordered the Apostles to be put outside for the deliberation.
Gamaliel warned those assembled against trying to kill the Apostles, because it might be unjust and therefore disobedience to God and defiance of Him.

Gamaliel gave an example of deceivers, namely "Theudas," who claimed to be a prophet or perhaps the awaited Messiah and made disciples of about 400 persons, but because he was false he perished and all his followers were scattered. So if the Apostles were deceivers like Theudas, God would destroy them and there was no need to kill them at the hands of the rulers.
Judas of Galilee: a person born in Galilee who raised a revolt against the Romans, refusing to pay them tribute, on the ground that the Jews were the people of God and paid tithes to God alone.

The taxing: this was a second census ordered by the emperor, different from the census that took place in the days of the birth of Christ, and its purpose was to register the subjects of the empire in order to collect tribute from them.
The Romans put down the revolt and killed Judas and many of his followers, and the rest fled and were scattered in many distant countries.
Gamaliel's purpose in this second example also was that the council should leave the Apostles alone, for if they were wicked, God would destroy them.
This counsel: the preaching of the Resurrection.
This work: the miracles.

Gamaliel asked them to leave the Apostles to speak about the Resurrection and work miracles, being sure that if the source of this work was a man, the work would come to an end in time, but if its source was God, He would establish it and no one would be able to fight it.

They agreed with him: the work of God was powerful, so the council was moved by Gamaliel's words and was persuaded by them, although there were other viewpoints, that there was no objection to disciplining the wicked, as they supposed the Apostles to be, but the grace of God made them silent and submit to his opinion.

Thus God used Gamaliel's wisdom to save the Apostles from being killed, but the high priest vented his anger toward them by flogging them, the custom among the Romans being 39 lashes, and he renewed his charge to them to stop preaching. By the flogging he meant to frighten them so that they would turn back from preaching Christ, or to put them to shame before the people after their flogging, because flogging among the Romans is a great disgrace, and so they would also be ashamed to preach.

Contrary to what the council expected, the Apostles went out in joy and zeal for greater preaching, because they regarded the pain of the flogging as fellowship in the sufferings of Christ and a preparation for the glories of heaven.
The Apostles continued steadfast in teaching in the Temple and in the houses in the name of the Lord.

Thus they set us an example in feeling the value of the spiritual mission and being concerned to accomplish it more than a man is concerned for his personal safety. They showed us that service is not only for those who attend church, but we seek out those far away and the sick in their homes and take every opportunity to serve Christ.
They held Liturgies and Christian rites in the houses, because churches had not yet been built.

If sufferings befall you because of holding to God's commandments or serving Him, may you accept them for the sake of His love, for if Christ sacrificed His life for you, it is not much for you to endure everything for Him, but to regard these sufferings as a blessing and an honor to you, because you shared with your Savior in carrying His cross.
The seven deacons
Multiplied: the number of Christians meant here is not specified, but the last figure St. Luke mentioned is five thousand (ch. 4:4), so the number must have been greater than that.
The disciples: a title given to Christians at that time because they were disciples of Christ and the Apostles, living a common life and all learning from the twelve Apostles.
Neglected: unintentionally, as a result of the large number and the Apostles' lack of time, so they forgot to distribute to some.
The daily ministration: the distribution of gifts was every day.

About 6 years after the founding of the Church, a problem emerged, which was the murmuring of the Jews of the Dispersion (who were abroad and had spoken Greek since the days of the Babylonian exile) against the Jews who had not left Jerusalem and spoke Hebrew, because the widows of the first group were not receiving enough of the daily distribution of material needs, and perhaps that made them feel like strangers, which increased their sensitivity.
The multitude of the disciples: the members of the Church in general, and especially those harmed by the poor and insufficient distribution.
It is not reason: that is, God does not accept and approve.
The word of God: preaching and teaching.
Serve tables: the distribution of gifts and material needs, called tables because the food is set on tables.

The conduct of the Apostle Fathers was exemplary, for they did not defend themselves or deny, but sought to solve the problem, explaining first that their ministry is essentially one of preaching and was commanded to them by Christ, therefore they would not leave it and be occupied with the ministry of distribution.

Look out among you: an application of the democratic system, so that the people feel their freedom, responsibility and participation in the organization of the Church, and consequently do not murmur afterward, because it was they who chose those responsible for distributing the gifts to them.
