The prophets of the Old Testament testified that whoever believes in Christ receives forgiveness of his sins, and this is another proof of the preaching of the Gospel in addition to the testimony of the Apostles who witnessed the resurrection.

This is the joyful message of salvation in which we have a share and an inheritance with all the saints, and which is the dearest thing we possess in the journey of our life on earth. Let us then be careful of it with all our senses, meditating on God’s love for us and thanking Him every day for His graces, and this will impel us to enjoy the relationship with Him and to rejoice in serving Him.

entries.section: (6) The descent of the Holy Spirit and Baptism

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter was surprised during his sermon by the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the hearers, as a declaration of their acceptance into the faith even before they were baptized, although Baptism is the entrance to the Christian life and after it the Holy Spirit descends in the sacrament of the Holy Myron. Here, however, the opposite happened, to declare a new truth to the minds of the Jews, namely the acceptance of the Gentiles like themselves into the faith.

entries.section: (6) The descent of the Holy Spirit and Baptism

paragraphs.text: The gift of the Holy Ghost: what is meant is the gift of speaking in tongues, as appears from the next verse. The Christians of Jewish origin, who had come with Peter from Joppa, were astonished at the acceptance of the Gentiles into the faith.

entries.section: (6) The descent of the Holy Spirit and Baptism

paragraphs.text: Peter’s companions saw and heard the Gentiles gathered in the house of Cornelius speaking in tongues and magnifying God, as had happened on the day of Pentecost, which was about eight years earlier while the faith was confined to the Jews, and Peter said that no one can forbid their baptism after the Holy Spirit has come upon them.

entries.section: (6) The descent of the Holy Spirit and Baptism

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Peter commanded that those gathered be baptized without circumcision, and the Christians of Jewish origin mingled with the Christians of Gentile origin in one common life for some days, after they had become one in Christ.
If you have been bound to the Church since your childhood, do not despise one who was far from it and joined it at last, for he may grow in his love for Christ and precede you into the Kingdom.
Do not boast of your origin or your religious knowledge, but humble yourself beneath the feet of all, and you will see Christ in them and learn from them.
Peter defends the acceptance of the Gentiles

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: The word of God: faith in Christ.
The rest of the Fathers the Apostles, members of the Mother Church in Jerusalem, heard of what had been done through Peter in the acceptance of the Gentiles, and this was not easy for them to accept.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: They that were of the circumcision: the Christians who had converted from Jewish origin.
Men uncircumcised: not circumcised, that is, Gentiles.
When Peter went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem, the Christians of Jewish origin objected to him strongly because of his mixing with the Gentiles, for this was against the Law of Moses.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Peter began to relate to them what had happened in order, to prove to them that the One who made the decision in that acceptance was God and not he.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Peter told them of his vision on the housetop in Joppa, where he saw the sheet coming down from heaven containing the animals, and God commanded him to eat of them because they are all clean, for they are God’s creation.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Peter objected because he did not eat the forbidden animals, so God confirmed their cleanness to him three times. Thus the symbols of the Jewish Law come to an end as the New Covenant begins.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Peter connected the vision with the arrival of the messengers of Cornelius immediately after it.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: The man: Cornelius.

The Holy Spirit commanded Peter to go with them without doubting the clear meaning of the vision, and he took with him six of the Christians of Joppa to testify before them to the truth of what had happened.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Their entering the house of Cornelius was a fulfillment of the command of the angel who had appeared to him, and not of their own personal opinion, in order to preach to them, great and small, the message of salvation.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: The beginning: the day of Pentecost, when the Church began with the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the disciples who were gathered.

The descent of the Holy Spirit upon the hearers during Peter’s speech was proof of the acceptance of the Gentiles, so Peter remembered the words of Christ about the baptism of believers in the New Testament with the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: The gift: the descent of the Holy Spirit and His gifts.

Could I withstand God: could I withstand God’s command to accept them into the faith, baptize them and mingle with them? If this was God’s decision, then no man, whoever he may be, is able to withstand God.

entries.section: (1) The dispute over the acceptance of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: They held their peace: they were convinced and no longer had any argument or objection with which to dispute.
They glorified God: a proof of complete conviction and then of rejoicing in the work of God.
Unto life: in the faith as members of the Church, and then the inheritance of eternal life.
The Church of Jerusalem was convinced and ceased from disputing, in submission to God’s command, and they began to glorify Him because He had accepted the Gentiles without circumcision.

Submit to the words of the Holy Bible and the teachings of the Church even if your mind does not grasp them, and then God will convince you because of your love and obedience to Him; and be diligent to carry out His word and to repent that you may enjoy life with Him.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Phenice: the meaning of its name is “land of palms,” and it is present-day Lebanon, and its most important cities are Tyre and Sidon on the Mediterranean Sea.

Cyprus: a fertile island in the Mediterranean Sea, now written (Cyprus). Antioch: it lies on the Orontes River in present-day Syria, and was built in 301 B.C. by the Greek Seleucids and named after Antiochus. It is considered the capital of the Church of the Gentile Christians, just as Jerusalem was the capital of the Church of the Christians of Jewish origin, and it was considered the third greatest city in the world among the Romans after Rome and Alexandria.

The believers, except the Apostles, were scattered from Jerusalem after the persecution that began with the killing of Stephen, and these believers moved to Phenicia, Cyprus and Antioch. They were preaching only to the Jews of their own nation.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Some Jews of Cypriot origin and from North Africa (Cyrene) were less fanatical than the Jews of Palestine, and when they reached Antioch they dared to preach Christ among the pagan Greeks, and God supported them in their preaching, so many believed.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: The tidings: that is, the spread of the faith not only among the Jews but also among the Gentiles in Antioch.

This news reached the Church of Jerusalem, so they sent Barnabas, who was a powerful preacher and teacher, to Antioch to help in the ministry, especially since he was Cypriot by origin and would be more acceptable to the Cypriots.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Full of the Holy Ghost: a good vessel in whom the Holy Spirit works with power in good works and effective preaching.

Barnabas came to Antioch and rejoiced over the new believers there, and exhorted them to stand firm in the faith with power; and because he was a good and wise man, this helped in spreading the good news and increasing the number of believers.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul was at that time in an unknown place in the city of Tarsus, which lies in Cilicia in Turkey, so Barnabas saw fit to have him share with him in the ministry of Antioch, because they had served together before in Jerusalem (ch. 9:27).

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Barnabas and Paul continued serving for a year in Antioch, and about ten years had passed since the crucifixion of Christ, and the good news had spread that made clear that Jesus is the Christ, so the believers were called Christians for the first time, after Christ the Redeemer. This shows us that the person of Christ was the center of the life of the believers and of the Church in Antioch at that time.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Prophets from Jerusalem: Christians from Jerusalem who prophesy. The Lord sent to the Church of Antioch believers who had the gift of prophecy.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: These believers prophesied that a great gathering would occur in the world, and this was fulfilled in A.D. 44 in the days of the Roman emperor Claudius.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Determined: the leaders of the Church in Antioch decided and commanded that gifts must be collected for the poor Christians of Jerusalem.
The disciples: the Christians, the believing disciples of Christ in Antioch.
According to his ability: according to the capacity of each person and his financial means.
Relief: an act of kindness.
The brethren: the Christians.

The love of the Church of Antioch appeared immediately, so they collected what could be collected to help the believers of Judea, whom the Jews were persecuting and whose property they often confiscated.

entries.section: (2) The extension of the ministry to Antioch

paragraphs.text: They sent what they had collected with Barnabas and Saul to Jerusalem. It is noticed that at this time Barnabas was named before Saul.
The offering reached the leaders of the Church of Jerusalem, whether apostles, bishops or priests, whom the Scripture calls the elders.

Barnabas was a great man of wide heart, who loved to share the ministry with others and not to confine it to himself, and even his possessions he had sold earlier and given to the Apostles (ch. 4:37). May God give us breadth of heart and love, which is the greatest of the virtues, so that we care to give to everyone in need, and share with those around us in working with us, putting them forward in honor so that they may be encouraged and rejoice in serving God. The martyrdom of James and the imprisonment and deliverance of Peter

entries.section: (1) The killing of James and the arrest of Peter

paragraphs.text: About that time: about A.D. 44, the time of the arrival of Barnabas and Saul with gifts for the poor Christians of Jerusalem.
Certain: some of the believers from among the ordinary members of the Church.

Herod: a name repeated in the Holy Bible. The first was Herod the Great (Mt 2:1-3), the killer of the children of Bethlehem, who killed his son Aristobulus. The second Herod is the killer of the Baptist (Mk 6:14), and the third Herod is the killer of the Apostle James (ch. 12:1-2), the brother of Herodias and son of Aristobulus, nephew of the second Herod and grandson of Herod the Great; he was called Herod Agrippa I, and his mother was Jewish.
Herod Agrippa began the persecution of the Christians in Jerusalem, and that was at the time of the arrival of Barnabas and Saul with gifts for the needy believers in Jerusalem.
This was the first Roman persecution of the early Church, because the previous persecutions were all Jewish.

entries.section: (1) The killing of James and the arrest of Peter

paragraphs.text: James the Apostle: one of the three who were closer to Christ than the rest of the twelve Apostles.
The brother of John: the Book of Acts was written after the death of James, and his brother John was still alive and well known, so it said “the brother of John.”
Herod seized James and killed him, thereby trying to win the Jews, and he cut off his head with the sword, as his uncle had done with John the Baptist.
Thus James drank of the cup as Christ had said to him (Mt 20:22), when his mother came asking a place for him at the right hand of the Lord.

entries.section: (1) The killing of James and the arrest of Peter

paragraphs.text: It pleased the Jews: in order to secure his kingdom, because he was an intruder upon the Jews, so he tried to please them by persecuting the Christians, whom the Jews hated because of their growth and their changing the customs of the Jews. Peter: one of the well-known leaders of the Christians, so Herod tried to kill him as he had James, in order to destroy the strength of the Christians by killing their leaders.
Herod wished to kill Peter, so he arrested him, and that was in the seven days of unleavened bread following the feast of the Passover.

entries.section: (1) The killing of James and the arrest of Peter

paragraphs.text: Four quaternions: each made up of four soldiers, two of them each bound to one of Peter’s hands and two guarding the door of the prison, and they were changed every three hours throughout the day, that is, four times, and this was repeated also at night.
To bring him forth: not for trial but for killing, like James.

Herod ordered that Peter be kept in prison under strict guard until the holy days of unleavened bread, on which killing is not permitted, were over, so that he might kill him after them. This shows Herod’s concern for the customs of the Jews in order to please them.

entries.section: (1) The killing of James and the arrest of Peter

paragraphs.text: Without ceasing: this shows how great the Church’s love for Peter was and its strong faith in God, who is able to rescue him. The Church had regained its composure after recovering from the sudden shock of the killing of the Apostle James, so it was raising prayers to God to rescue Peter. For the Church has no power with which to face the world except the power of prayer.

Do not be disturbed by the violence of others’ wrongs against you, but lift your heart in prayer, confident of the power of God that supports you; for though He allows some trials for your benefit, He is able to stop the wrongs of others, and He cares greatly about your prayer because He loves you and is able to protect you.

Sleeping: this was at the end of the night, that is, the fourth watch, because the guard soldiers change every three hours and did not know that Peter was not there until the morning (v. 18), so it was in the last shift of the watch, which is before dawn.

The Lord waited, in His providence, until the night before the day when Herod was about to kill Peter, and Peter was deeply asleep in peace and complete trust in God; he was bound to two soldiers by both hands, while the other two soldiers were guarding the door.
The house: the prison.

God sent the angel to bring Peter out of the prison instead of the soldiers who were leading him to be killed, so the light of God shone in the place, and the angel struck the side of Peter, who was deeply asleep, to wake him, then called him to rise quickly, so that he would not doubt what he saw, and he rose to go out of the prison; and the chains of his hands fell off by themselves without the two soldiers noticing.
The angel asked Peter to put on his clothes and his sandals quietly and follow him, and Peter thought that he was in a vision.

The angel passed with Peter the first guard post and then the second, since he was confined in the inner prison, then they came to the outer gate, which also opened by itself in complete quiet, and when they had gone out of the prison the angel went with him along one of the streets of the city, then disappeared from him so that he could complete his way to the house.
Was come to himself: he became fully alert and realized what had happened to him.

Of a surety: he was certain that God had brought him out of the prison and rescued him from death. The expectation of the people of the Jews: who hated him and wanted to be rid of him. Here Peter realized the truth of his deliverance by the angel from the hand of Herod and the Jews.
When he had considered the thing: aware of all that had happened to him.
The house of Mary: it was the meeting place of Christ with His disciples, where He ate the Lord’s Supper and appeared to them after His resurrection, and where the Apostles were accustomed to gather.
John, whose surname was Mark: John is his Jewish name and Mark is his Greek name, and it was customary for a person to have two names in those times.
Praying: that God would rescue Peter.
The porch: the passage that leads to the outer door of the house.

Peter came to the house of St. Mark, where the believers were gathered for prayer all night, and when the maid “Rhoda” came to find out who was knocking at this hour, and recognized Peter’s voice, she was overwhelmed with joy so that she did not open the door but went back inside to tell those gathered of the miracle.
Thou art mad: her mind has become disordered and she is speaking untrue words.
Constantly affirmed: she was aware and certain that the voice was the voice of Peter, whom she knew well because of his frequent visits to this house.

Here we see something strange: the praying believers had faith in the power of prayer, but it was not enough to believe the answer; and since the believers held that each person has a guardian angel, they accused the maid of raving, supposing that the one standing at the door was Peter’s guardian angel who had come to comfort them.
Peter continued knocking, so they opened and were astonished when they saw him.

Peter asked them to be quiet and told them the story of his coming out of the prison, and asked them to inform James the Less the Apostle (the son of Alphaeus), one of the twelve, because he was the bishop of Jerusalem, and likewise to inform the rest of the believers of what had happened. And he went out to another place to hide there from the spies of King Herod.
No small stir: not only because of Peter’s disappearance, but because they expected severe punishment from Herod that might reach the point of killing them.
What was become: how Peter had disappeared, because they had not felt him go out and there were no traces showing how he got out of the prison.
When the sun rose, the soldiers were greatly disturbed because they did not find Peter in the prison.
Examined: he questioned the guards to learn how Peter escaped from the prison.
Should be put to death: when he failed to learn which of them had helped Peter escape, he ordered them to be killed for not keeping Peter, who escaped from them.
Caesarea: a great city in Judea on the coast of the Mediterranean, in which the force of the Roman authority was stationed.

Herod did not find Peter to kill him, so he ordered the soldiers to be killed, because Roman law decreed that the guard should suffer the punishment that would have befallen the one he was guarding if he escaped from him.
After that Herod left Jerusalem and came to Caesarea, where he stayed for the remainder of his life, which was very short.

God’s arrangements, for the course of events is not by the mere effort of man but by God, who permits and arranges everything according to His divine plan; so Peter was delivered and Herod is the one now about to die. Do not be disturbed if the wicked rise up against you or the events of the world press in on you, because God is able to rescue you from them and to change all the events around you.
Them of Tyre and Sidon: the people of Tyre and Sidon, which are cities on the coast of the Mediterranean in present-day Lebanon.
With one accord: it seems they were not in agreement, but out of fear of poverty and hunger they agreed to win Herod’s favor so that he would restore trade with them.
The king’s chamberlain: the one responsible for his palace and its guarding, who is of course trusted by the king and close to him.
Their country was nourished by the king’s country: it depended on trade with the lands subject to Herod.

Herod was angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon because of their commercial competition with the city of Caesarea, and they found that they had to appease him because of their great need to deal with the lands of Judea, since their land was commercial and not agricultural, and they were also small cities in which living required trading with Judea.
A set day: one of the feast days of Caesarea on the occasion of its founding.
When Herod put on his shining, splendid royal robe and sat on his throne in pride, addressing them with a pardon for them, these pagans began to flatter him, regarding him as a god and not a man.

Herod’s heart was lifted up and he believed the praise of the Tyrians that he was a god, and he did not give the glory to God, the Creator of all, so He struck him with worms to eat his flesh while he was alive, which is a matter of the utmost difficulty and pain, so he died a very horrible death, at the age of 54, in the fourth year of his reign.
The word of God: the preaching of Christ.
Here we come to the close of the chapter that began with the killing of James and the imprisonment of Peter, to see the death of Herod and the spread and growth of the preaching.
Ministry: delivering the gifts of the Church of Antioch to the needy among the believers in the Church of Jerusalem.
After Paul and Barnabas had been present at these events in Jerusalem, they returned to Antioch and took with them John (St. Mark), the son of Barnabas’s sister.

Do not be proud, however great your strength or authority, for God is longsuffering and able to punish the wicked, but He is patient with them that they may repent. So be humble, and do not be troubled because of your weakness, confident of the power of God that supports you; for as He supported the early Church, He is ready to uphold you with His grace and satisfy you with His love.
Barnabas and Paul on the first journey

Prophets: they either speak of things that will happen in the future, like Agabus, who prophesied that a famine would occur in Jerusalem (ch. 11:28) and about the arrest of Paul there also (ch. 21:10, 11), or they speak about the Kingdom of Heaven, which is the future of our life as believers; that is, they preach and encourage the hearers to prepare for eternal life.

With this chapter the acts of the Apostle Paul begin, whereas the first part of the book concentrated on the acts of the Apostle Peter. Here we see the beginning of the work of Paul and Barnabas together on the first journey. The first journey includes the preaching of Paul and Barnabas in Syria, Turkey and Cyprus, traveling by sea and by land.

The journey began from Antioch, the first center of the Church of the Gentiles, which was full of many teachers such as Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger (the Black), Lucius of Cyrene (North Africa), Manaen who had been brought up with Herod Antipas the second, the killer of the Baptist, and Paul.
Ministered to the Lord: they led the prayers and carried out teaching and visiting of the believers and caring for them in Antioch.

Fasted: this shows the importance of fasting and prayer and that they are among the foundations of worship in the early Church. The Holy Ghost said: He declared to the leaders of the Church in some way, whether by an angel or a voice or any other way.
During the fasting and prayers of the Church, the Holy Spirit asked for Barnabas and Saul to be set apart for a special ministry of preaching, namely preaching to the Gentiles in many other lands.
Fasted… prayed: this shows the importance of joining fasting with prayer in worship, and also as a preparation for any ministry.

Laid their hands on them: this shows the importance of the authority of the Church in directing servants to service, for although the ones being sent were Barnabas and Saul, the Apostles who lead the Church, they do not move except by the direction of the council of the Church.
The believers fasted and prayed, asking the Lord’s help for them, and laid their hands on them for blessing.

The first journey began from Antioch (Syria) by land to Seleucia (Syria), then by sea to Salamis (Cyprus), and after that by land to Paphos (Cyprus), and after that to Perga in Pamphylia (Turkey), then by land to Antioch of Pisidia (Turkey), followed by land to Iconium (Turkey), then by land to Lystra (Turkey), which is the town of the Apostle Timothy, the disciple of Paul, and in which Paul healed the lame man and was stoned. After that he went by land to Derbe (Turkey) and from there to Lystra (Turkey) by land, then also by land to Iconium (Turkey), and after that by land to Antioch of Pisidia (Turkey) and from there to Perga (Turkey) by land, then by land to Attalia (Turkey), and after that by sea to Seleucia (Syria), and finally he returned to Antioch (Syria) by land, where the journey had begun.
This journey took the period from A.D. 45 to A.D. 48, and is recorded in chapters (13-14) of this book.

Great is the planning of the Holy Spirit, who, if a person entrusts his life to Him, produces great fruit. So seek God’s counsel before any work, and offer many prayers and join them with fasting as much as you can, especially before great undertakings.

Being sent forth by the Holy Ghost: a confirmation that God sent them, and that their mission was not of themselves. Seleucia: a port of Antioch on the Orontes River, about 16 miles west of Antioch. Cyprus: an island in the Mediterranean Sea belonging to the Roman Empire, with many Jews in it, which was distinguished by fertility and prosperity at that time; it is present-day Cyprus.

The two Apostles came to the island of Cyprus because it was the birthplace of Barnabas (ch. 4:36) and of some of the believers of Antioch, and it is not far from it (about 50 miles), so they began preaching there.
Salamis: a city in the southeast of Cyprus and the most important of its commercial ports.
As was the custom of the two Apostles, they began proclaiming the good news to the Jews in the synagogue at Salamis, and with them was St. Mark, surnamed John, a disciple to both of them.

Gone through the isle: they went from Salamis in the southeast of the island westward toward Paphos, a distance of about 100 miles, knowing that the length of the whole island is 150 miles, so they most likely passed through its towns preaching Christ until they reached Paphos.
Paphos: a port in the southwest of the island of Cyprus, famous for the worship of the goddess Venus, and in it was the seat of the Roman authority.
Barjesus: the meaning of his name is son of Jesus (Joshua).
Paul and Barnabas crossed the island by land to Paphos, where they found a Jew who claimed prophecy and practiced sorcery, whose name was Barjesus.
Which was with the deputy: Barjesus was one of the close counselors of the deputy, because Sergius was a lover of knowledge, so he was interested in the prophecies of Barjesus and his sorcery.
Called for Barnabas and Saul: when the two Apostles began to preach, the deputy, a lover of knowledge, heard of them, so he wanted to know the new teaching they were preaching.
Desired to hear the word of God: regarding it as a new teaching that he wanted to become acquainted with.

The deputy Sergius was a man who sought the truth, so he was dazzled by the miracles of that sorcerer even though he was a philosopher and thinker, and when Paul and Barnabas came, he asked them to let him hear their message.
Withstood them: by disputation and mockery, relying on the deputy’s confidence in him.

Elymas: that is, one of much knowledge; it is an Aramaic name and title of the sorcerer Barjesus and has its meaning in the Arabic language. To turn away the deputy from the faith: the deputy began to be convinced by the preaching of the two Apostles, so the sorcerer tried to confuse his thoughts and cast doubt on him so that he would not believe in Christ.

Saul, who is also called Paul: he had two names, and hence his name was called Paul, which is his Latin name, because he had begun preaching to the Gentiles, so it seemed good that his name should be acceptable to them. Set his eyes on him: he looked intently at him in order to judge and punish him and to alert those present to what he would say to him. Here we see Saul (the Hebrew name, meaning “asked for”) and his Latin name Paul (that is, “little”), filled with the Holy Spirit, who supports him in his ministry, and he goes ahead of Barnabas for the first time in acting.
All subtilty: the sorcerer relied on deceit to convince his hearers of his words.
Child of the devil: because Satan is a liar and the father of lies.
Enemy of all righteousness: he resists the word of righteousness that the two Apostles preach and tries to turn people away from faith and godliness.
Wilt thou not cease: a rhetorical question to rebuke Elymas for persisting in evil.
Paul declared the wickedness and evil of that sorcerer and his opposition to the true work of God.
The hand of the Lord is upon thee: God punishes you so that you may repent.
For a season: a temporary period, that perhaps he may repent.
A mist: his sight became very weak.
Darkness: he lost his sight completely.
Sought some to lead him by the hand: he was unable to move by himself, that perhaps his feeling of weakness might lead him to repentance and the rejection of pride.

Paul asked God that Elymas the sorcerer be struck with blindness for a season until he should repent, so he immediately began to grope in the darkness, deprived of light, just as he wanted to deprive the deputy of the light of faith, and he did not know how to move.

Astonished: at the power of the preaching of the two Apostles and the immediate carrying out of the punishment on the greatest of his sorcerers and counselors, being certain of the truth of the new teaching because of its superiority and its evident power over the teaching of the deceiving sorcerer.

Truly, what a man sows, that he also reaps. Whoever lights the way of others, God lights his way, and whoever works for their going astray, his own going astray returns upon him. So be concerned to do good and to help those around you, and keep away from condemnation and from any evil, however persuasive it may be or however much the circumstances around you help toward it, and be confident that good is rewarded in the end with very many blessings.
Perga in Pamphylia: Pamphylia is a province in the west of Cilicia in present-day Turkey, and the city of Perga is the capital of Pamphylia.

The two Apostles moved by sea to the coasts of Turkey, and here St. Mark parted from the two Apostles and returned to Jerusalem and left them. Luke did not mention the reason for the parting, but we learn later that the Apostle Paul was troubled by this, while Barnabas made excuses for him and disagreed with Paul after a while because of what Mark had done (ch. 15:37-39); but the Apostle Paul came back and showed his love and trust in him (2 Tim 4:11).

Pisidia: a province lying north of Perga, whose capital is the city of Antioch, which is different from the city of Antioch that lies in Syria, and the road to it from Perga is mountainous and rugged and has many robbers, so the two Apostles were exposed to many dangers, which they endured, trusting in God.
Went into the synagogue: in the city of Antioch of Pisidia there was a large number of Jews and of Greeks who had become Jewish proselytes.
Sat down: in the place where the teachers sit, since it was customary for Jewish preachers and teachers to pass through the synagogues in different lands and preach in them.
Paul and Barnabas and those with them moved on, passing through Perga without preaching in it, and came to Antioch of Pisidia and entered the synagogue to begin preaching in it as was their custom.

Men and brethren: it was evident from the appearance and clothing of the two Apostles that they were strangers, but knowledge showed in them, and their sitting in the place of the teachers showed that they were Jews versed in the Holy Scriptures and able to teach.
After the reading from the books of Moses and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue asked them to give a word of exhortation if they wished.
Then Paul stood up: here Paul continues to go ahead of Barnabas in speaking and preaching, although the latter was known for preaching, but Paul excelled and became famous for it.
Beckoning with his hand: that they be silent and pay attention to what he would say.
Men of Israel: the Jews, the children of Israel.

Ye that fear God: the Greek proselytes who love to hear Jewish teachings and have not yet become Jews. Paul began his first recorded sermon in the Holy Bible, and it closely resembles the sermon of the martyr Stephen, in that it reviews the whole history of the Jewish nation up to the coming of Christ, His crucifixion and His resurrection.
Chose our fathers: Paul spoke as a Jew, so he called the fathers “our fathers,” and by the fathers he means Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and his twelve sons.
Exalted the people: He blessed them with abundance of offspring and strength.
With an high arm: he means the ten plagues and the dividing of the Red Sea.

Their manners: their murmurings, their attempts to return to Egypt and their refusal to enter the Promised Land. Paul spoke about God’s choice of Abraham and his offspring, their sojourn in Egypt and their departure from it by the miracles of God, then their journey in the wilderness for forty years, which was full of murmuring.

When the children of Israel reached the Promised Land in Canaan, Joshua divided among them the land of seven nations, namely the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, after destroying these peoples. The land of Canaan was the lowland west of the Jordan, and the land of Aram is the highland east of the Jordan.

The children of Israel did not drive out all the wicked inhabitants of the land, being lax in carrying out Joshua’s commandments, so they rose against them and occupied them and humbled them, and they cried out to God, who sent them judges who delivered them, and this was in what is called the age of the Judges, which lasted 450 years, and the last of these judges was Samuel the prophet.

The children of Israel asked Samuel to choose a king for them, so he was angry and rebuked them because God is their King, but God agreed in order to satisfy them, and gave them Saul the Benjamite, whom they had asked for, and he ruled them for 40 years.
God rejected King Saul because of his evil, and anointed David as king by the hand of Samuel. David was obedient to God and his heart was pure like His, and he walked according to His will.

God promised to raise up a Savior from the seed of David, and He fulfilled this, giving to His people Israel Jesus Christ as Savior (2 Sam 7:12, 13, 16; Ps 89:36-37). This verse is the goal of the sermon of the Apostle Paul, and what precedes it is a preparation for it.
Fulfilled his course: he completes his ministry and his preaching after baptizing people unto repentance.

John the Baptist, known among all the Jews for his greatness and the truth of his words, prepared for the coming of Jesus Christ with the baptism of repentance, confessing his weakness before the great Christ who was coming after him.
Brethren: a gentle expression of love toward the Jewish hearers that draws them to faith.
Children of the stock of Abraham: the Jews who take pride in their sonship to Abraham.
Whosoever among you feareth God: he means the Greek proselytes who love to hear Jewish teachings, that is, the Gentiles who love God.
The word of this salvation: the preaching of Christ the Savior.
Paul began gently inviting his hearers, Jews and Gentiles, to accept faith in Christ the Savior.
Knew him not: they did not understand that Jesus is the awaited Messiah, because they supposed that the Messiah was an earthly king and not a spiritual one.
The voices of the prophets: which show that the Messiah would suffer and die for His people.
Condemned him: that He deserved death.
The Jews who dwell in Jerusalem, where the Temple is, rejected faith in Jesus Christ and persecuted Him, and even condemned Him to death, and thus they fulfilled the prophecies of the prophets.

The Jews of Jerusalem tried to catch any fault in Christ throughout His life and did not find any, and His righteousness and innocence were proved; yet, in their wickedness, they asked Pilate the governor to kill Him.

The tree: the Cross. After the chief priests completed the agreement with Judas, the disciple of Christ, to betray Him, they seized Him and struck Him and mocked Him and crucified Him until He died and was buried in the tomb.

The Jews thought they had gotten rid of Christ, but they were surprised by His resurrection on the third day. He said: “God raised him,” meaning by that that the Father by His will and the Son by His divinity raised His body from death on the third day.
Many days: forty days.

Them which came up with him from Galilee: the twelve and the Apostles and many of His disciples and followers. Christ confirmed His resurrection by appearing many times during forty days after His resurrection to His disciples, who preach in His name and bear witness to His resurrection.
The promise: God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and all the fathers of the Jewish nation of the awaited Messiah.
As the Apostles preached in Jerusalem and Judea, so Paul and Barnabas now preach in Antioch of Pisidia to fulfill God’s promise of salvation for the whole world in Christ Jesus.

Paul cited the second Psalm, which spoke of the divinity of Christ, and that He is the eternal Son of God who was born as an incarnate man at a specific time to save the world; this God has fulfilled for us in these days by the redemption of Christ, His death and His resurrection.
No more to return to corruption: He does not die again like those raised from the dead, such as Lazarus, the daughter of Jairus and the son of the widow of Nain.
The sure mercies of David: God’s promises to David of the salvation that is accomplished in Christ and that we receive in the Church of the New Testament.
Christ rose from the dead with a resurrection after which there is no death, to give human beings the enjoyment of the mercies of Christ, the Son of David.

David mentioned in (Ps 16:10) that His body, that is, the body of Christ, would not see corruption, and of course this is about Christ and not about David, who died and was buried with his fathers and whose body decayed after he had completed his service as king; but Christ is the One who rose and saw no corruption.
Be it known unto you: to show the importance of the following words.
By him: faith in Christ.
The law of Moses: it shows sin and its punishment and the reward of carrying out the commandment, but it is unable to justify man; the One who justifies us is Christ alone, by His blood.

This is the message of forgiveness, that is, escape from punishment, and of justification, that is, innocence and deliverance from evil. Thus through Him we escape from the daily dominion of sin and from its eternal punishment, which the Law was unable to grant us.
Ye despisers: those who refuse to obey the word of God, whether in the days of Habakkuk or at the preaching of Christ.
Wonder: you do not believe and understand.

Perish: the coming of divine punishment upon the Jews in the days of Habakkuk, or the killing of the Jews in Jerusalem in A.D. 70. A work in your days: the destruction that comes upon those who reject faith.

A work which ye shall in no wise believe, though a man declare it unto you: a terrible destruction for those who reject the word of God, whether by the Babylonian captivity in the days of Habakkuk or the destruction by the demolition of the Temple and Jerusalem in A.D. 70, and all this is a warning of the terrible torment in the eternal fire.

The Apostle Paul warned them against treating the message lightly, lest there be fulfilled in them the saying of the prophets in “Hab 1:5” about those who are lax in their life with God, so the Babylonian captivity came upon them as a discipline for them, and unfortunately they did not believe his prophecy until they actually perished at the hands of the Babylonians. We note that twenty years after this sermon, destruction and ruin came upon Jerusalem at the hands of the Romans.
This is the message of salvation offered to us for our benefit.

God is calling you to repent, so do not reject His voice sent to you in the Holy Bible and on the lips of the Fathers and teachers in the Church. The opportunity of repentance is available now so that you may enjoy His forgiveness, and He will even pour out His grace upon you and rescue you from eternal destruction.

entries.section: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

paragraphs.text: After the end of the sermon, the hearers were moved, especially the Gentiles, that is, the devout Greeks who love to attend the synagogues of the Jews and listen to the sermons but had not yet become Jews, and they expressed their longing for the new teaching by asking the two Apostles to complete their teaching on the coming Sabbath, which is the time of the weekly meeting in the synagogue.

entries.section: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

paragraphs.text: The religious proselytes: the Greeks who love to hear Jewish teachings in the synagogue. The hearers who admired the words of the two Apostles did not wait for the coming Sabbath to hear about Christ, but followed the two Apostles, and those who followed were not only Gentiles but also Jews, and they used to go to them in the house where they stayed to hear their teachings; and the two Apostles seized these opportunities and went on confirming their faith in Christ, which had begun within them.

entries.section: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

paragraphs.text: Almost the whole city: not only the Jews but also the pagan Gentiles, for most of the city’s inhabitants were pagans.

Envy: since they felt that the Jewish teachings had not attracted the pagans as the new teaching did, and because they regard the Jews as distinct from the Gentiles, how could they now be equal in the Christian faith. Spake against: they present arguments against the new teaching to cast doubt on it.

Contradicting: declaring that the right teaching is the Jewish one and showing the error of the new teaching. Blaspheming: declaring that the awaited Messiah is not the weak Jesus who suffered and died. When very many people gathered at the synagogue on the following Sabbath, the Jews were jealous of the success of the two Apostles, and began to oppose them and to blaspheme against the preaching.

entries.section: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

paragraphs.text: Waxed bold: he was not afraid but declared the right teaching and the danger to the Jews in their opposing it.

It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: it is God’s will that the Jews be preached to first about Christ, because they are the people of God who know the prophecies and are awaiting the Messiah, so they would have a greater readiness for faith.
Put it from you: you rejected faith.
Unworthy of everlasting life: you will receive the punishment of rejecting faith, which is eternal torment. We turn to the Gentiles: the focus on preaching to the Gentiles.
A light of the Gentiles: Christ is the light of the whole world, and His Apostles and servants preach Him to the Gentiles and bring them out of the darkness of sin into the light of faith.
For salvation unto the ends of the earth: the salvation of Christ is offered to the whole world and not only to the Jews.

The two Apostles confronted them with the fact that their rejection of the word of God confirms their unworthiness of it, and that they would preach to the Gentiles according to the prophecy of Isaiah the prophet (Isa 49:6) on the right of the Gentiles to salvation.

entries.section: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

paragraphs.text: That: that is, salvation is offered to the Gentiles as to the Jews.
Glorified the word of the Lord: they held fast to the faith and thanked God.
The Gentiles rejoiced greatly and many believed who were known to God by His foreknowledge and who have a share in eternal life, and the word of the Lord spread in the region.

entries.section: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

paragraphs.text: Stirred up: they spoke against the two Apostles and showed the error of their teachings, and stirred up the women and the rulers of the city against them.

Devout women: those of pagan origin who were interested in attending the synagogue of the Jews and hearing its teachings, whether they had become Jewesses or were still pagans and only loved to hear Jewish teachings. Honourable: the rich who held a high position in society.

The chief men of the city: the great and elder men of the city who influence the leadership of society, and they are probably relatives or acquaintances of the honorable women, so they were influenced by their words.
Persecution: in the form of rebuke and mockery.
Expelled them: they drove them out of the city with contempt.
The Jews pushed forward some of the Gentile women who had standing in society, and they stirred up a persecution against the two Apostles and drove them out of the city.

entries.section: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

paragraphs.text: Against them: a testimony against the Jews who drove them out that they reject faith.
Iconium: a city in Asia Minor southeast of Antioch of Pisidia, 50 miles away from Antioch.

The two Apostles fulfilled the commandment of Christ to shake off the dust of their feet against the city (Lk 9:5), declaring that they sought no personal benefit from the preaching, so they took nothing from the city, not even the dust of the ground, then they came to Iconium also in Turkey.

entries.section: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

paragraphs.text: The disciples: those who believed in Christ and became His disciples, since the Christians were called disciples.
The new believers were exceedingly joyful in the faith and in the work of the Holy Spirit despite the tribulation and persecution.
Our Christianity is able to gladden our hearts whatever troubles we find in the world.
Let us hold fast to God’s commandments even if others oppose us, and offer our love and our service to all without ceasing, for in the end they win hearts.
The rest of the first journey
The Greeks: those who attend the synagogue of the Jews and heard the two Apostles and believed in Christ.
Made their minds evil affected: they stirred them up against the two Apostles and their teachings, saying that they oppose their religion and cause disorder in the city.

The Gentiles: the pagan Greeks in the city who do not attend the synagogue of the Jews and hold fast to their paganism; and for the sake of evil the wicked Jews united with the pagans in hostility to the two Apostles so as to be a force to resist the preaching of Christ.

The brethren: the Christians who believed, whether from the Jews or the Greeks. The Jews who rejected the faith were greatly troubled that Jews like themselves had believed in Christ, and they call the Greeks who believed in Christ brethren, because by this they feel that they have lost their distinction as the chosen people of God, since they used to despise the Gentiles. In the city of Iconium the preaching began in the synagogue of the Jews as usual, and many Jews and proselytes believed, which stirred up those of the Jews who did not believe, so they began to deceive the Gentiles with corrupt words and to push them to oppose those who had believed.
Abode they long time speaking boldly: the two Apostles were not afraid of the opposition of the Jews who rejected faith in Christ, and continued preaching to the Jews and the Gentiles with courage.
Gave testimony unto the word of his grace by: 1- the convincing proofs in the words of the two Apostles.
2- the joining of many to the faith.
3- the working of various miracles such as healing the sick and casting out demons.
Signs and wonders to be done by their hands: miracles to confirm the faith of those who believed and to draw others to faith, and trust in the word of God on the lips of the two Apostles.
A division occurred among the people of the city, as some of them were on the side of the Jews and others on the side of the two Apostles.

Both of the Gentiles, and also of the Jews with their rulers: the unbelieving Jews united with the Gentiles who held fast to their paganism, under the leadership of the rulers of the Jews and the rulers of the Gentiles.
An assault: the planning of a plot to attack and arrest the two Apostles.
To use them despitefully: to wrong them and accuse them of being wicked, saying that they had stirred up the city and were preaching wrong ideas, namely their claim that Jesus is God.
To stone them: their intention was to sentence them to death by stoning.
They were ware of it, and fled: not out of fear, but to continue preaching and winning souls for Christ.
Lycaonia: a province or district in Asia Minor, that is, present-day Turkey.
Lystra: a large city in the south of Lycaonia about 40 miles from Iconium.
Derbe: a large city in Lycaonia about 25 miles from Lystra.
The region that lieth round about: it is clear that the two Apostles, on their journey to Lystra and from it to Derbe, preached in the lands through which they passed.

It is beautiful for a person not to be hindered by negatives but always to strive for what is positive. If a door is closed before you, do not be troubled, but look for the open door and continue in your service and faithfulness in your work and love for those around you.
Never had walked: this shows his permanent disability for many years, and that there was no medical treatment that would benefit him.
In the city of Lystra there was a man who had been lame from his birth.

The same heard Paul speak: it seems that they used to put this lame man in one of the marketplaces, so Paul took this place, where many gather, to preach in it; and this lame man, who sat there to beg, paid attention to Paul’s preaching and listened to him.

Perceiving that he had faith: signs of conviction by Paul’s words appeared on his face, in addition to the gift of the Holy Spirit in the sacrament of the priesthood, which helped Paul to understand and know his readiness and faith.
With a loud voice: this shows Paul’s authority in healing, and to alert all those present to the miracle so that they would believe.
Leaped: jumped, and this shows that he received strength in his muscles that enabled him not only to walk but also to jump, and this shows the power of the miracle.
Paul called the lame man to stand on his feet, and he leaped and was healed immediately.
What Paul had done: he commanded the lame man, with authority, to stand, and he stood at once.
Lifted up their voices: they cried out in a loud voice and glorified the gods.

In the speech of Lycaonia: their local language; and at the same time they knew the Greek language in which Paul was preaching because it is the language spread throughout the whole world, but when a person is excited he speaks spontaneously in his original language however well he knows the foreign language.

The crowds of hearers were dazzled and spoke in the local language, which the two Apostles did not understand, and this confirms that the Holy Spirit had not given them the gift of speaking in tongues or interpretation in this situation, because they were speaking in the Greek language; and they said that Paul and Barnabas were the gods Hermes and Zeus. Hermes was the Greek god of eloquence and his symbol was the planet Mercury, and Zeus was the god of the gods and his symbol was Jupiter, and they believed that Hermes was the interpreter and the spokesman for Zeus, so they thought that Paul was Hermes because he preaches and speaks more than Barnabas, and Barnabas was Zeus, the god of the gods and the foremost of all the gods.
Before their city: where a statue or temple of the gods stands.
The gates: the gates of the city near the temple of the gods.

The people: this shows that the people of the city were all, or at least mostly, pagans. The priest of Zeus came with oxen, which are the greatest of the sacrifices, and garlands, which are used in the worship of idols, to offer them to the two Apostles.

Heard of: at first the two Apostles did not understand the speech of the crowd because it was in a language strange to them, but when they saw the crowds moving toward the gates of the city and preparing the oxen and the garlands, they asked what was happening, and they told them of their belief that they were the gods Zeus and Hermes and that they wanted to offer them the worship and honor that befit them.
Rent their clothes: a Jewish custom, also found among some peoples, as in Upper Egypt, as an expression of great grief or distress.
Crying out: they had to cry out because the crowd was speaking and even shouting, so they were forced to cry out so that they would hear them.
Why do ye these things: they rebuke them for trying to offer worship to them.
Of like passions with you: exposed to hunger, thirst and sickness, and therefore we are not gods, because gods are not exposed to the troubles of men, as the pagans believe.
These vanities: the pagan worship.
The living God: not like the lifeless idols that neither speak nor move.
The two Apostles declared to the crowds that they were men like them, and that they were preaching to them the worship of the one God the Creator and not these many vain gods.
In times past: from the beginning of creation to the Incarnation of Christ.
Suffered: He was longsuffering toward the peoples of the world.

Their own ways: the mistaken pagan worship, from which they did not turn back even though it wearied them greatly. God left the Gentiles, from the creation of the world to the coming of Christ, to walk in their own ways, and chose only the Jews as a people for Himself.

He left not himself without witness: God declares Himself to the Jews through His speaking with the prophets, but He shows Himself to the whole world through the conscience, which is the voice of God within every person, and through His good gifts that He bestows on the whole world, for they all testify to His existence and His love.

Rain: it waters man, animals and plants, so the deserts are built up and God’s love appears. Fruitful seasons: weather conditions that help the plants to grow, so they give fruit that man and animals eat.
Food and gladness: when a person finds his food, he rejoices and enjoys it, and he should then thank God, who gave him his material needs and gladdened his heart.
With these sayings: by their declaring that they were men and that God is far higher than they supposed and that He is the doer of good to mankind.
The two Apostles were able, with difficulty, to keep the crowds from offering sacrifices to them.
Jews from Antioch and Iconium: those who rejected faith in Christ and drove Paul and Barnabas out of their cities.

Persuaded the people: that Paul and Barnabas speak wrong teachings and curse the gods because they said that their worship is vain, and even claim that a man called Jesus is God; and perhaps they attributed the miracle of raising the lame man to the Apostles’ relationship with Beelzebub, as they had accused Christ before.
Stoned Paul: they struck him with stones until he fell to the ground wounded and unconscious.
Drew him out of the city: so that the wild beasts would eat his corpse, as contempt and abuse of him.

Jews arrived from Antioch of Pisidia and Iconium and stirred up the crowds, and they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city after they thought he was dead, so that he would not be buried in the city and become famous by his body as a great teacher.
The disciples: those from Lystra who believed and became disciples of Christ.
Rose up: it seems he was unconscious from the violence of the stoning and then recovered, and perhaps God gave him strength and healing so that he was able to stand and walk.

The next day: the very next day, so the wicked who thought they had killed him did not notice him, and he left Lystra quickly because there was no opportunity for service in it at that time, and headed to a new place to preach in it. Barnabas: it is evident from the foregoing that Barnabas was not harmed because of his silence, whereas Paul, because of his much defending and preaching, was exposed to death.

When the Christians surrounded Paul they found him alive, so he rose and came with Barnabas to Derbe. We note that Paul faced the stoning which he used to be glad to carry out against the Christians, such as Stephen, to whose stoning he was a witness before he believed.

The opinions of people are changeable, so do not cling to them; for after they honored the two Apostles they rose against them to kill them. Care about God’s opinion of you even if people object, and do not please others at God’s expense, but hold fast to His word however great the pressures on you.

entries.section: (3) In Derbe, then the return to Antioch

paragraphs.text: That city: it is Derbe, and those who opposed him in Lystra did not follow him.
Taught many: no opposition to the ministry is mentioned in this city, so many believed and became disciples of Christ.

They returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch: the courage of Paul and Barnabas appears in their returning to the lands from which they had been driven out and where they had even been plotted against to be killed; but most likely they did not preach openly among the crowds, but met with the believers and confirmed them in the faith.
The two Apostles began the preaching in Derbe, and many believed, then they returned to Lystra, Iconium and Antioch.

entries.section: (3) In Derbe, then the return to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Confirming: they encourage the believers because of the great harassment from the wicked around them. Through much tribulation: it is a proof of man’s love for God and his holding fast to Him and his not clinging to the world. The kingdom of God: the heavenly Kingdom.
The two Apostles went on confirming the faith of the disciples and making clear to them the importance of enduring tribulations to receive salvation.

entries.section: (3) In Derbe, then the return to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Had prayed with fasting: this shows the importance of fasting and prayer in choosing priests and preparing them for service. The two Apostles did not choose priests when they began preaching in these cities, either because they were driven out and had no time to ordain priests, or they may have postponed the ordination of priests until the Church grew, even a little, and someone appeared in it who was worthy of this rank in terms of his spiritual readiness and his bearing the responsibility of service. Commended them: they regarded these churches as a deposit which they placed in the hand of God, in whom they trusted that He would keep them and make them grow.

The two Apostles appointed priests (the word means, from the Syriac qashishu, elders), and the people used to elect them and then the Apostles would sign them with the cross; and they organized the ministry in the churches, and prayed and fasted with them, then left them in the care of God.

entries.section: (3) In Derbe, then the return to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Pisidia: after they had confirmed the believers in Antioch, the capital of Pisidia, they passed through the province of Pisidia, and perhaps they preached in some of these lands.
Pamphylia: a province in Asia Minor next to Pisidia.

Preached the word in Perga: it seems that they did not preach in Perga, a large city in the province of Pamphylia, when they visited it the previous time (ch. 13:13), but now they preached Christ in it. Attalia: a port in Asia Minor to which the two Apostles went in order to sail from it to Syrian Antioch. The two Apostles passed through Pisidia to Pamphylia and preached in Perga, then came to the port of Attalia.

entries.section: (3) In Derbe, then the return to Antioch

paragraphs.text: Recommended: the Church had sent them for preaching and committed them into the hand of God, who blessed their journey and made it successful.
The work which they fulfilled: the preaching in the cities through which they passed during their journey.
The two Apostles sailed back to Antioch of Syria, where they had begun their journey, by the grace of God.

entries.section: (3) In Derbe, then the return to Antioch

paragraphs.text: When they arrived at Antioch, they gathered the believers and told them of God’s work with them on the journey, and that God had called many of the Gentiles to faith.

entries.section: (3) In Derbe, then the return to Antioch

paragraphs.text: After the first journey, which took about three years and began in A.D. 45, they stayed two years in Antioch with the believers as they had been before the journey; that is, they served two years in the Church of Antioch in Syria.

When a person finds that he has completed what the Lord asked of him, he is made very happy and thanks God for what He accomplished for him and through him. So, my brother, be careful to complete every service and responsibility given to you, because it is from God and you will give account for it before Him, and then He will help you and gladden your heart.
The Council of Jerusalem and the beginning of the second journey

From Judea: where Jerusalem is the center of Jewish worship, so those who believed in Christ there feel responsible for caring for the rest of the churches in the world because Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, and because they still held fast to the Law of Moses that they had lived by all their lives and were unable to perceive that it was a symbol and a preparation for Christianity.

Some Christians of Jewish origin came, who had not been convinced by the vision of Peter and the Baptism of Cornelius, and who afterward became roots of the Ebionite heresy that appeared at the end of the first century and from which the Adventists or Sabbatarians are now descended; these came from Jerusalem to Antioch teaching the Christians of Gentile origin that they must be circumcised and keep all the Jewish rituals in order to receive salvation.

Dissension and disputation: the discussion became heated between Paul and Barnabas on the one hand and the Christians of Jewish origin who came from Judea on the other, and they did not reach any agreement. They determined: those gathered from both parties agreed to return to the leadership of the Church represented in the Apostles, who made Jerusalem their center and go out from it to preach and then return to it. This is what is mentioned in (Gal 2:1-9) that Paul went up to Jerusalem by a divine revelation, that is, that God commanded him to go to Jerusalem to obtain a decision from the council of the Apostles in this matter, and those gathered agreed to that. Certain other of them: delegates from the Church of Antioch.

The elders: the priests, that is, the priests who assisted the Apostles. Here it appears that the leadership of the Church is the council of the Apostles and priests, which is now the council of bishops called the Holy Synod.

Paul and Barnabas strongly opposed those who came from Judea, then they arranged that they should go up with some Christians of Antioch to the Apostles and the priests in Jerusalem to examine this matter.

Great joy: the Christians in Lebanon (Phenicia) and the northern part of the land of the Jews (Samaria) were not fanatical for the Law of Moses, because they had long been lax in holding to it, so they rejoiced at the faith of the Gentiles without their becoming Jews.

Paul and Barnabas went out, officially sent by the Church of Antioch to Jerusalem, and passed through Phenicia and Samaria, and told of the faith of the Gentiles and their joining the Church, and the believers rejoiced at that.

The two Apostles and those with them arrived at Jerusalem, and its Church welcomed them as an official delegation from the Church of Antioch, and they told everyone the news of the first journey and how many of the Gentiles believed, were baptized and became Christians; and this news came before the convening of the council and as a preparation for it.

Many came who had been Pharisees originally, that is, holding fast to the Law of Moses, and they began to oppose the words of Paul and those with him about the faith of the Gentiles, and proclaimed the importance of circumcision and the Law for the believers of Gentile origin to be saved.

Here we see the breadth of heart of the Church, for it does not reject an opinion except after discussion and prayer and conviction of what is right and without arbitrariness, and this is the sound method in leading the Church so that everyone is convinced and a chance is given to the heretics to repent.

May you apply this in your home so that you win all the members of your family, and respect the opinions of your children even if they are small, and convince them of what is right with longsuffering.
The apostles and elders: whether those in Jerusalem or those who came from the neighboring lands of Judea, and by this they formed the first council in the history of the Church in A.D. 50.
A council of the Apostles and priests was convened, and many discussions took place among them about whether circumcision and the Law are necessary for the believers or not.

Much disputing: at the beginning of the council, the discussion continued for a long time between Paul and those with him and the Christians of Jewish origin, on the importance of circumcision and the Law for salvation. A good while ago: about 10 years ago, when Cornelius was preached to in Caesarea.
Peter rose to present his point of view, since he was the first to preach to the Gentiles by divine revelation when he preached to Cornelius and those with him.
Which knoweth the hearts: He who knows the readiness of the hearts of men for faith.
Bare them witness: by the preaching of Peter.
Giving them the Holy Ghost: whose gifts appeared in their speaking in tongues, so they received the same power of the Holy Spirit that the Christians of Jewish origin received.
Peter explained how the Holy Spirit descended on the Gentiles before they were baptized, to show God’s approval of their Baptism without circumcision or keeping the commandments of the Law.
The faith of the Gentiles in Christ has purified their hearts, with no difference between them and the believers from the Jews.

Tempt ye God: we set conditions for salvation that God did not set, for He required faith, Baptism and life in the Church, and did not ask Christians for circumcision and the Law. If God has accepted the Gentiles, how can we ask them for a proof of their faith, namely circumcision and keeping the Law? By this we are tempting God, especially since the Jews were unable to keep the whole Law, so how can we demand it of the Gentiles.
The grace of the Lord Jesus: which gives faith and the Holy Sacraments. We shall be saved: we Christians of Jewish origin.
Even as they: the Christians of Gentile origin.
The grace of God is what saves everyone through faith.
The hearers kept silent, as a sign of their agreement, and Paul and Barnabas began to describe the miracles that had been done among the Gentiles through them on their journey.
Encourage those far from God to join the Church, showing God’s love for all, especially sinners. Do not demand many things of them, and give an opportunity for their love to move first toward God.

James: he is James the son of Alphaeus, one of the twelve Apostles, the son of the maternal aunt of Christ and the bishop of Jerusalem, the writer of the Epistle of James, called the Just, and he is the president of the Council of Jerusalem. St. James spoke and asked everyone to listen.

The Apostle James made clear that God had accepted the Gentiles into the faith at the hand of Peter when he baptized Cornelius and those with him, then confirmed His acceptance of them at the hand of Paul and Barnabas when they preached and founded churches among the Gentiles.

After this: after the Jewish worship deviated into preoccupation with the letter and not the spirit, and indeed the Jews were neglectful and busied themselves with their desires, so the Jewish nation was exposed to captivity and the destruction of the Temple. The tabernacle of David, which is fallen down: he means the Tabernacle of Meeting, that is, the Jewish worship that deviated and fell in the sight of God.
I will build again the ruins thereof: this worship was destroyed, but God restores it and completes it through Christian worship. The residue of men: those other than the Jews who live around them.

The Gentiles, upon whom my name is called: all human beings are created in the image and likeness of God, and they are the children of God, and He calls them in the fullness of time to faith in Christ.

Who doeth all these things: He who created mankind and chose the Jews as a people particular to Himself, then became incarnate and accomplished redemption and receives the Jews and the Gentiles into faith in Christ.
Known unto God: all the foregoing is in God’s plan from eternity, to redeem all mankind and receive them into faith in Him.

James declared that the acceptance of the Gentiles was prophesied by the prophets, as in (Amos 9:12, 11), that God will rebuild the Jewish Church that went astray, and then will receive the Gentiles also, because God is for all and calls all, for He is their Creator, and this is His eternal plan.
Trouble: the Christians of Gentile origin are being required to fulfill the Law of Moses in order to be saved.
Which are turned to God: those who leave the worship of idols to believe in Christ.
James declared that his opinion is not to require circumcision and the Law of the Christians of Gentile origin.

Blood: the Law of Moses forbade the drinking of blood (Deut 12:16), and so does Christianity, because blood represents the life of a person, so whoever drinks blood is as if he sheds the blood of another and treats his life lightly, and this actually used to happen when a man killed another and drank of his blood in revenge on him, and still today we find one threatening another with the words (I will drink of your blood). James was content to require the Christians of Gentile origin to abstain from taking part in the feasts of the unclean idols and from practicing fornication, which was a part of idol worship, and from eating strangled animals because their blood is still in them, and likewise from drinking blood, both of which are among the prohibitions of the Law.
Moses: he means the five books of Moses, which forbid fornication and the drinking of blood.
Of old time: for hundreds of years.
In every city: the cities to which the Jews emigrated, and likewise in the cities of Judea, they established synagogues in which the Holy Scriptures are read.
Every sabbath day: the day of rest that is set apart for worship and attending the synagogues.

It is known in the whole world through the synagogues of the Jews that the Law forbids eating what is strangled and blood, so the Christians of Gentile origin must be committed to not eating or drinking blood and likewise to not committing fornication, like their brethren of Jewish origin, for this is necessary for all Christians, because blood stirs up desire and fornication is a grave sin.

Keep away from mixing with the wicked lest you share in their sins, and open your heart in love to everyone in general relations, praying for them and committed to good conduct, and you will be an example for all.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: Chief men among the brethren: to confirm the decisions of the council, for they were not content to send a letter lest some doubt that it was forged by Paul and Barnabas.
Barsabas: that is, son of Saba.
Silas: who is also called Silvanus.

The Apostles and the priests and the whole Council of Jerusalem decided to send delegates with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch to represent the Church of Jerusalem, and they were Judas surnamed Barsabas and Silas, who became the companion of the Apostle Paul on his second journey, and they were well-known believers.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: The council gave the delegates sent to the churches of Syria and Turkey a letter carrying the decisions of the council, and began it by sending greeting.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: Subverting your souls: they cast doubt on the believers and caused disturbance in their souls.

The council made clear that the Christians of Jewish origin who went from Jerusalem to Antioch and proclaimed the necessity of circumcision and keeping the Law for believers of Gentile origin, these were not sent by the Church in Jerusalem.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: Being assembled with one accord: after dialogue and differences of opinion, they agreed on one opinion.

Our beloved: to show the degree of the Apostles’ trust in and love for Paul and Barnabas, and therefore in their teaching. The opinion of all agreed to send two men with Barnabas and Paul, whom the Apostles describe as having risked death for the preaching of Christ, and they would tell them the decision of the council orally also.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: Things offered to idols: not only the meats, but all the corruptions connected with these feasts.
Ye shall do well: the sound conduct that is commended before God.

James declared the decision of the council, which resulted from the meeting of the Holy Spirit and the Apostles and the priests, the leaders of the Church, showing that God is the One who leads the Church through prayer and guides it in all its affairs. The decision was not to require of them anything except abstaining from eating what is sacrificed to idols, from drinking blood, from eating what is strangled, and from fornication.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: The delegates arrived with the message of the council at Antioch, so they gathered the members of the Church and delivered the letter to them.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: When the letter was read, the believers rejoiced and were comforted by it, as they became sure that their faith was sound and that they did not need circumcision and the Law, and the dispute and clash in the Church ended and the barrier between the Christians of Jewish and Gentile origin was removed, and they saw the support and joy of the Mother Church in Jerusalem in them, and this was an encouragement to the spread of the Church among the Gentiles in the whole world.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: Prophets also themselves: prophecy in the New Testament means telling of the future, which is the Kingdom of Heaven, that is, preaching and teaching preparation for eternal life.
Judas and Silas began to preach to the people in Antioch and to encourage them in the spiritual life and confirm them in the faith.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: After Judas and Silas completed their mission in Antioch, the Church sent them off in peace to return to the Apostles in Jerusalem.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: It seems that some of the believers held on to Silas so that he would stay with them, so he did not return with Judas to Jerusalem and continued serving in the Church of Antioch.

entries.section: (4) Communicating the decisions of the council

paragraphs.text: Paul and Barnabas continued to complete their ministry in the Church of Antioch which they had begun before going to Jerusalem and its council, and with them were many servants who preached in Antioch and the lands around it.

The one Holy Spirit leads the Church through its bishops and priests. May you be committed to the mind of the Church and not to your personal opinions, and if you are perplexed about something, return to the Fathers of the Church and its servants so that you may live by the one Spirit and devote yourself to growing in the love of God.

entries.section: (5) The beginning of the second journey

paragraphs.text: Some days after: it is thought to be about a year that Paul and Barnabas spent in the service of the Church of Antioch after the Council of Jerusalem, that is, they began the second journey about A.D. 51.

After about a year, Paul suggested to Barnabas that they make a second journey to visit those whom they had preached to on the first journey, and to check on their condition. This points to the importance of visitation in following up the effect of the word of God.

entries.section: (5) The beginning of the second journey

paragraphs.text: Barnabas thought that they should take Mark, the son of his sister, with them on the second preaching journey as on the first.

entries.section: (5) The beginning of the second journey

paragraphs.text: Paul did not agree, because Mark had not completed the first journey with them, but returned from the province of Pamphylia to Jerusalem.

entries.section: (5) The beginning of the second journey

paragraphs.text: As a result of the difference between Paul and Barnabas (which was without hatred or ill will, since Paul commended Barnabas in (1 Cor 9:6), and commended Mark in (2 Tim 4:11 and Col 4:10-11), each of them went to preach with another companion. Thus two teams were formed for preaching instead of one team, and Barnabas traveled with Mark to visit Cyprus, the original homeland of Barnabas, and there they preached until Barnabas was killed by being beaten with sticks.

entries.section: (5) The beginning of the second journey

paragraphs.text: Recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God: they bade him farewell with prayers, that God might keep him during his preaching journey.
Paul went with Silas to serve in Syria and Turkey (Cilicia).

If a difference of opinion occurs with those around you, do not lose your peace, and take care that the result is a positive one with which God is pleased even if it differs from your thinking and planning, for God turns everything to good for those who love Him.
